title: Renew a Nigerian Passport: 2026 Fees, NIN Check and 21-Day Target
summary: To renew or reissue an existing Nigerian passport, use the NIS official passport portal's Apply for Renewal/Reissue route, verify NIN and date of birth, enter your current passport data, choose a processing centre and booklet, then upload supporting documents, pay and book an in-person biometric appointment. NIS's revised April 2026 agreement still lists ₦100,000 (32 pages/5 years) or ₦200,000 (64 pages/10 years) for domestic applications, excluding bank charges, and a reissue service target of 21 days after successful biometric enrolment.
feeLabel: Inside Nigeria: ₦100,000 (32 pages/5 years) or ₦200,000 (64 pages/10 years)
feeNote: The April 2026 NIS SLA lists domestic standard-passport prices of ₦100,000 and ₦200,000 for the two common booklet options, excluding bank charges. The September 2025 NIS press release lists diaspora prices of $150 and $230; confirm the current category-specific amount on the official portal or mission. Renewing a passport does not automatically incur the ₦30,000 correction-of-data administrative fee, which applies to a separate service where relevant.
timeline: NIS's April 2026 SLA lists 21 days after successful biometric enrolment for a standard-passport renewal/reissue. The target does not include time waiting for an appointment and is not a guaranteed passport collection date. Check the application's actual NIS status before travel.
requirements: Your existing Nigerian passport and legible data-page details, including the booklet for presentation at the biometric appointment. A missing or stolen passport may require the separate lost-passport replacement route.
Your NIN slip or official NIN verification details matching the application. NIS compares current passport identity with your NIMC details and asks for a date-of-birth check.
An NPC birth certificate or High Court declaration of age and local-government/indigene or state-of-origin document if requested by the official NIS renewal checklist.
An ICAO-compliant passport photograph for the NIS upload and a valid personal email, contact address and next-of-kin information.
Any additional documents specific to the renewal reason; an actual name, marital-status or other biodata correction uses NIS's change-of-data process and its own evidence/administrative charge.
The official payment amount and access to the application acknowledgement, receipt and biometric appointment slips.
steps: Open https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and select Apply for Renewal/Re-issue, not Apply for Fresh Passport or Correction of Data. If you are applying from outside Nigeria, choose the overseas application path and check the Nigerian mission's instructions.

Verify the NIN using the requested date-of-birth check and enter the current passport booklet/data-page details. Compare the returned NIMC identity fields with the existing passport; do not create inconsistent information to get through validation.

Confirm that your case is an ordinary expired/expiring renewal. If the passport is lost/stolen or you need to change a name, date of birth or marital status, use the relevant NIS replacement/change-of-data guidance because the evidence and administrative charges can differ.

Choose the processing centre and 32-page/5-year or 64-page/10-year booklet. Check appointment availability, upload a compliant photograph and supply the birth/origin and supporting documents requested for your application type.

Review your personal details, contact/next-of-kin information and passport data-page evidence. Correct any error through the proper responsible authority before final submission rather than paying for an application based on contradictory records.

Pay through the official NIS checkout and book the biometric appointment. Domestic baseline booklet fees are ₦100,000 and ₦200,000 excluding bank charges; check the live checkout total for your selected route, then save/print the receipt, acknowledgement and appointment slip.

Attend the selected Immigration Office in person on the scheduled date with your current passport booklet and required originals. NIS requires a photograph and biometric data capture even after online submission and payment.

After biometric enrolment, return to https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and open Application Status/Print Receipt for the same submission. Use the application identifiers from the original acknowledgement to check the actual status, and ask the selected passport office about collection once it confirms issuance. The 21-day NIS reissue target starts after successful enrolment and is not a promised pickup date.
notes: Ordinary renewal of expired/unexpired validity and correction or replacement for loss are not interchangeable. Consult the appropriate NIS guide if you have changed personal information or cannot present the existing booklet.

Do not infer a ₦30,000 correction-of-data administrative fee for every simple renewal from the table of additional services. The official portal determines the charges applicable to the particular application.

The revised April 2026 NIS SLA retained a 21-day target after successful enrolment for reissue. It is not a guarantee that a booklet can be collected on a precise date or a promise of an appointment within 21 days.

NIS asks renewal applicants to upload a compliant photograph and relevant civil/origin evidence and appear with the current booklet for biometric capture. A fully remote renewal is not established by the official guidance.
Passport fees quoted in naira apply to applications within Nigeria. NIS has published distinct US-dollar amounts for applications abroad; verify current mission and payment requirements.

title: First Nigerian Passport: Application, ₦100,000/₦200,000 Fees and Requirements
summary: First-time Nigerian standard-passport applicants should start on the official NIS passport portal, choose Apply for Fresh Passport, verify their NIN and date of birth, select a processing centre and booklet, upload the required birth/citizenship documents, then pay and book biometric enrolment. The April 2026 NIS Service Level Agreement lists ₦100,000 for 32 pages/5 years or ₦200,000 for 64 pages/10 years for applications inside Nigeria, excluding bank charges, and a 42-day service target measured after successful biometric enrolment—not after payment.
feeLabel: Inside Nigeria: ₦100,000 (32 pages/5 years) or ₦200,000 (64 pages/10 years)
feeNote: NIS's April 2026 SLA confirms the domestic standard-passport amounts ₦100,000 and ₦200,000, both excluding bank charges. NIS's published announcement separately lists $150 and $230 for those booklet categories for applications abroad. These are official published rates rather than a guarantee of the exact checkout for every location or citizenship category; confirm the current payment on NIS's own portal and never pay an intermediary.
timeline: The revised April 2026 NIS SLA lists a target of 42 days after successful biometric enrolment for a fresh standard passport. It is a service target, not an appointment wait-time or guaranteed ready-for-collection date. Track status using NIS after enrolling, especially before making travel plans.
requirements: A NIN slip or other identity verification evidence requested by the official NIS portal. The application checks NIN-linked date of birth and displays NIMC personal details for review.
An NPC birth certificate or High Court declaration of age, plus local-government/state-of-origin/indigene evidence applicable to the citizenship category and processing centre.
An ICAO-compliant passport photograph for portal upload. Check NIS's photo-compliance tool and any additional printed photographs or guarantor documentation required for your citizenship category.
A working personal email address, contact/residential address and next-of-kin information for the NIS form and application notices.

For applicants under 18: parent/guardian consent, evidence of the parent's Nigerian citizenship and the child's birth certificate; NIS lists additional court/state ministry documents for adopted children.

For applicants whose Nigerian citizenship is by naturalisation or registration, the relevant Presidential naturalisation/registration certificate and any category-specific identity/guarantor evidence. The domestic NIS portal directs these categories and adopted/surrogacy cases to NIS Headquarters Abuja.
Funds for the exact official booklet selection, bank charges and a means to save or print the application acknowledgement, payment and biometric appointment evidence.
steps: Open https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and select Apply for Fresh Passport. Check the domestic/overseas route first: the domestic portal offers an Apply from outside Nigeria option and not every applicant category is processed at the same location.

Use the official NIS dashboard to verify your NIN and the required date-of-birth match. Carefully compare the displayed NIMC name/date details with your genuine birth and citizenship records; resolve material inconsistencies through the relevant issuer rather than inventing new details in the form.

Choose the correct processing centre and passport booklet size—32 pages/5 years or 64 pages/10 years—and prepare a compliant photograph. Check centre appointment availability on the official NIS portal before making time-sensitive travel arrangements.

Enter your contact address, next-of-kin details and valid email. Upload the NPC birth certificate or accepted court declaration and the state/local-government origin or citizenship evidence NIS requests for your applicant category.

Before submission, check the category-specific document list. A minor may need parental citizenship documents and consent; naturalised/registered citizens and adoption/surrogacy categories have additional requirements or processing-location limits. Do not assume an adult citizen-by-birth checklist is sufficient for every applicant.

Review the application in full, submit through NIS's own portal, pay the amount the portal quotes and book the available biometric enrolment appointment. NIS's published domestic baseline is ₦100,000 or ₦200,000, excluding bank charges; do not pay a personal bank account or an unofficial agent.

Save or print the payment receipt, application acknowledgement and appointment slip. Attend your selected Immigration Office personally on the appointed date with all original evidence requested by NIS; photograph and biometric data capture cannot be completed simply by uploading online.

After successful enrolment, monitor the official application status/receipt route and follow NIS's specific collection instructions. The April 2026 SLA states a 42-day target after enrolment, not a promise that the passport will be ready exactly 42 days after online submission.
notes: Fresh passport and renewal/reissue are different routes. An applicant with an existing valid or expired passport should normally use Renewal/Reissue; replacing a lost booklet or changing personal data may require a separate documented process.

Domestic NIS passport fees are published as ₦100,000 and ₦200,000 for the two common booklet options, exclusive of bank charges. The official NIS fee announcement lists separate dollar-denominated diaspora amounts; check current portal/mission instructions before paying abroad.

A successful online payment or booked appointment is not a completed passport application. The applicant must attend physical biometric/photo enrolment, and the published 42-day service target begins after successful enrolment.

NIS lists additional rules for minors, adopted children and citizens by naturalisation or registration. Verify your own category rather than uploading guessed or unrelated affidavits or using a generic adult checklist.
Check the exact online portal status and official collection instructions. Do not purchase travel tickets on the assumption a published service target is a guaranteed issuance date.

title: Nigerian Passport Change of Data: Official Cost, Documents and Timeline
summary: Use the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) passport portal to request correction of passport details, then attend an appointment with your existing booklet for biometric capture. NIS's April 2026 service agreement lists a ₦30,000 correction-of-data administrative charge, but that is not necessarily the whole passport payment. Its timetable is conditional: a combined fresh/change-of-data row says 42 days after enrolment, while the specific correction row says 21 days if marked NLO. Confirm the processing category and current total with NIS rather than assuming either target is guaranteed.
feeLabel: ₦30,000 administrative correction charge; other passport/processing charges may apply
feeNote: NIS's April 2026 Service Level Agreement lists a ₦30,000 Correction of Data administrative charge, and its table also lists passport booklet prices of ₦100,000 (32-page, 5-year) or ₦200,000 (64-page, 10-year) for the domestic table, exclusive of bank charges. It does not make the ₦30,000 charge an all-inclusive correction quote. NIS's own checkout determines the applicable total, route and booklet options; verify it before paying. Embassy/consular charges can differ abroad.
requirements: Current passport data page and the physical passport booklet for the required appointment and biometric capture.

NIN slip with identity details that can be checked against the passport application; resolve material NIN/civil-record discrepancies through the responsible authority before submitting conflicting corrections.
Birth certificate issued by NPC or a declaration of age from a High Court, as specified by the passport service.
Local government or state of origin/indigene certificate and a compliant passport photograph where requested by NIS.
An application letter explaining the exact correction, supported by a court affidavit for the routes that require it.
A newspaper publication for the change-of-name/correction types NIS lists, including replacement, addition, deletion or rearrangement of names.
Additional evidence for the specific situation, such as a marriage certificate for a change related to marital status; the required paperwork varies by correction category.
Means to pay through the legitimate NIS checkout and save the appointment, acknowledgement and payment slips.
steps: Start at https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and choose Apply for Correction of Data (not Fresh Passport or ordinary Renewal/Reissue). Check that the domestic or overseas application pathway matches where you will attend biometrics.

Before payment, identify which passport entry is wrong and collect the existing booklet, NIN slip and relevant civil records. A marital-status change, name reordering and a data-entry correction can have different evidence requirements on NIS's official Passports page.

Complete the correction application with the details you can support. Select the passport processing centre and review every field against the NIN and civil records to avoid paying for a new mismatch.

Upload the specific required evidence: NPC birth certificate or High Court declaration, origin/indigene certificate, signed reason-for-change letter, affidavit/newspaper notice and marriage certificate as applicable. Do not present a marriage certificate as universally mandatory for unrelated corrections.

Review the full amount requested on the NIS official checkout and pay only there. The 2026 service agreement mentions a ₦30,000 administrative charge alongside separately listed booklet prices, so do not treat ₦30,000 as a universal final payable amount.
Book the available appointment and save the acknowledgement, payment and appointment slips. Bring your existing passport booklet and any originals that NIS instructs you to present.

Attend the selected immigration office on the date scheduled for photo and biometric capture. Nigerians applying from abroad should use the relevant embassy, High Commission or consulate arrangements; no online form alone completes the identity-capture stage.

After successful enrolment, use the official passport portal's application-status/receipt option to follow progress. NIS's April 2026 agreement displays different conditional 21- and 42-day targets, so confirm which one the processing office applies to your case.
notes: The 2026 NIS agreement contains two timing entries: the general fresh/change-of-data line shows 42 days, but a separate correction-of-data line states 21 days after successful enrolment '(IF NLO)'. This guide deliberately discloses both rather than misrepresenting a single guaranteed turnaround.

The ₦30,000 fee is the stated administrative charge, not proof the full cost of a replacement booklet or bank processing is ₦30,000. Check the official portal amount, and retain only the acknowledgement NIS actually generates.

NIS distinguishes correction of errors, change in marital status and replacement/addition/deletion/rearrangement of names. Document requirements can vary, so use the checklist for the precise correction rather than assuming every listed document applies universally.

NIS requires an in-person biometric/photo appointment with the current passport booklet. Nigerians abroad should follow embassy/consular instructions for where to submit the application and attend enrolment.

NIS's April 2026 SLA supersedes the previously cited 2025 edition for this fee/timeline comparison. Targets are measured after successful enrolment and do not guarantee a collection date; check status before planning travel.

title: How to enrol for a NIN
summary: Get a first National Identification Number through NIMC's free enrolment process. Citizens and legal residents of any age are eligible; NIMC captures demographic information, performs age-appropriate biometric checks and de-duplicates the record before issuing an 11-digit NIN. Registration, a transaction slip and an issued NIN slip are distinct stages.
feeNote: NIMC's current NIN and fees pages state that enrolment and obtaining a NIN are free.
requirements: Eligibility as a Nigerian citizen or legal resident

Applicant demographic and contact details collected during enrolment; NIMC does not publish one universal supporting-document list for every applicant category, so follow the exact centre/self-service prompt for the identity record it requests
A valid civil or identity record appropriate to the enrolment category, particularly for a minor, checked against the centre's published requirements.
Access to an official NIMC enrolment centre or authorised front-end partner; biometric or identity verification must be completed by the applicant, not a paid agent.
steps: Open NIMC's official NIN page and Find an Enrolment Centre directory to choose a recognised centre/front-end partner. New NIN enrolment and issuance are free.

Confirm the correct category for an adult, child or legal resident and ask that centre about acceptable birth/identity documents before travelling; NIMC does not publish one universal list for every case.
At the authorised enrolment centre, provide the applicant's full legal name, date/place of birth and other requested details. Review the display before submission.
Complete the photograph, fingerprint and digital-signature capture appropriate to the applicant's age and circumstances; NIMC runs a duplicate identity check before issuing a NIN.
Keep the Transaction Slip and any acknowledgement. This is not automatically the final NIN slip, and successful data capture does not guarantee immediate issuance.
Return through the centre's official follow-up/collection instructions for the issued NIN slip. NIMC says NIN collection requires biometric verification and cannot be delegated to a proxy.
If there is a duplicate or identity mismatch, contact NIMC or the enrolment centre with the transaction reference rather than starting another paid registration or changing details informally.
notes: NIMC says citizens and legal residents from birth are eligible and ordinary enrolment and NIN issuance are free.
A NIN is unique for life. Do not publish it together with a name and contact details on social media.
NIMC distinguishes the transaction slip from the NIN slip after processing and requires the owner's biometric verification for collection.

title: How to change your date of birth on NIN
summary: Correct a date of birth already attached to an existing NIN through NIMC's official self-service or authorised assisted modification route. The required NPC digitised birth certificate or attestation must support the date. NIMC currently publishes conflicting prices of ₦28,574 and ₦15,000; verify the live authorised invoice, not a third-party quote.
feeNote: Fee shown follows NIMC's dedicated current Fees page. An older modification detail page still shows the former ₦15,000 amount, so confirm the amount generated by the official payment route before completing payment.
requirements: Existing NIN
Digitised NPC birth certificate for applicants born after 1992, or digitised NPC attestation certificate for applicants born before 1992
Access to the NIMC self-service modification account or an official NIMC enrolment/modification centre
Payment through the official NIMC modification route
The exact existing date on the NIN record and correct date supported by an NPC digital birth certificate or an eligible NPC attestation.
A working NIMC self-service account or access to an authorised modification centre; keep payment and transaction references.
steps: Before paying, compare the existing NIN details against the legal civil record. If the NPC birth record is itself wrong, use NPC's correction route rather than uploading conflicting dates.
Check whether the applicant has the appropriate digitised NPC birth certificate or attestation. NIMC's guidance distinguishes people born before 1992 from those born later.
Open https://selfservicemodification.nimc.gov.ng/ or NIMC's linked modification route and authenticate the existing NIN account. Use an authorised NIMC centre if self-service is not accessible.

Choose Date of Birth modification (not ordinary name, phone or address modification). Compare the displayed price against NIMC's fee schedule and any official payment invoice before authorising payment.
Enter the certificate number and requested civil-record details, upload legible evidence and check the preview to avoid changing a correct field inadvertently.
Submit the correction request and retain the official transaction/payment reference. A submitted or paid application is not evidence that the underlying identity record has already changed.
Monitor the NIMC request status and respond to any official document query. After approval, retrieve the updated NIN slip and verify the corrected birth date.
If NIMC's older ₦15,000 page conflicts with the current ₦28,574 fees page or the generated invoice, use NIMC customer support to confirm the amount. Never pay an intermediary's personal bank account.
notes: NIMC's official fees page states ₦28,574 for date-of-birth modification, while its older adults modification page still states ₦15,000; retain the editorial conflict until NIMC aligns these official pages.
Date of birth is separately charged, not part of the ₦2,000-per-updatable-field standard category.
A correct NPC record and completed payment do not automatically approve the NIMC modification.

title: How to get a new Nigerian driver's licence
summary: A first Nigerian driver's licence requires accredited driving-school training, a certificate number, the official FRSC application and payment, State Board of Internal Revenue confirmation, VIO driving test and personal FRSC biometric capture. The fee depends on Class A versus other classes and a three- or five-year term.
feeNote: FRSC lists Class A at ₦7,000 for 3 years or ₦11,000 for 5 years; other classes at ₦15,000 for 3 years or ₦21,000 for 5 years. Payment-channel charges may apply.
requirements: Applicant must be at least 18 years old
Completed training at an accredited driving school
Driving-school certificate number used to initiate the fresh application
Personal/contact details plus the processing centre, validity period and licence class selected in the FRSC application form
Proof of completing accredited driving-school training and the certificate number that FRSC asks for at fresh-application entry.
Ability to attend the VIO test and FRSC Driver's Licence Centre for photograph/fingerprint capture; a third party cannot do the biometric stage.
steps: Confirm that the candidate is at least 18 and has completed training with an FRSC-accredited driving school. Obtain the school's driving certificate number.
On the official Nigeria Driver's Licence portal select a fresh application and enter the school certificate number to begin, not Renewal or Reissue.
Select the correct licence class, three- or five-year validity and preferred processing centre. Check contact and personal details before moving to payment.
Review FRSC's price table: Class A ₦7,000/₦11,000 and other classes ₦15,000/₦21,000 for three/five years respectively, with possible extra channel/class charges.
Pay only through the FRSC portal or a participating bank identified by it; preserve the application ID, receipt and appointment instructions.

Take the application and payment receipt to the State Board of Internal Revenue desk associated with the selected Driver's Licence Centre. Ask the BIR desk to validate the official payment, then attend the Vehicle Inspection Officer's practical driving test at the VIO test location given by the centre.
Attend the selected FRSC Driver's Licence Centre in person for photograph and biometric capture; keep the acknowledgement or temporary licence documentation issued.
Use FRSC Track DL Application Status for the real stage of printing/collection. Contact the processing centre if the record stalls rather than paying someone who promises faster approval.
notes: FRSC's official price table separates Class A and other classes as well as three- and five-year validity.
The original training certificate is used to initiate fresh registration; simply paying online is not completion of driving competence testing.
Fresh licensing differs from renewal of an expired existing licence or reissue of a valid one.

title: How to renew a Nigerian driver's licence
summary: Renew an expired licence through FRSC using the existing driver's-licence number, date of birth and selected class/validity. Licence fees depend on class, additional classes and payment channel. The online payment step is not proof that FRSC has completed any required photograph, biometric or collection stage.
feeNote: FRSC lists Class A at ₦7,000 for 3 years or ₦11,000 for 5 years; other classes at ₦15,000 for 3 years or ₦21,000 for 5 years.
requirements: Existing driver's licence number
Applicant's date of birth used to access/edit the application
Updated personal/contact details where needed
Chosen processing centre, licence class and 3-year or 5-year validity option
The expired original driver's-licence number and date of birth for the correct FRSC record.
Current photograph/biometric attendance and collection evidence if the FRSC application dashboard or centre requires it.
steps: Verify that the licence is actually expired. FRSC distinguishes Renewal of an expired card from Reissue/Upgrade actions for a still-valid card that needs another class.
On the genuine FRSC Driver's Licence portal open DL Application → Renewal and find the correct existing licence record using licence number and date of birth.
Update personal/contact details, selected processing centre, class and validity (three or five years). Do not inadvertently change the holder or select the wrong class.
Check the payable charge in FRSC's table and official checkout, noting that multiple classes and payment-channel charges can increase the cost.
Complete payment through the official authorised route and keep the acknowledgement, application ID and transaction receipt.
Follow any FRSC directions to attend the chosen Driver's Licence Centre for biometric recapture or other identity/testing stage. Another person cannot provide your biometrics.
Track status using the FRSC Track DL Application Status option with application ID or existing licence number and date of birth.

When FRSC marks the card ready, contact the selected centre for collection requirements. If payment succeeded but no application exists, report the payment reference to official FRSC support before repeating payment.
notes: FRSC lists ₦7,000/₦11,000 Class A and ₦15,000/₦21,000 other-class fees for three/five years on its official FAQ.
A renewed card still requires actual issuance and, when instructed, in-person biometric processing.
Renewal is not interchangeable with the route for changing classes on a still-valid licence.

title: How to replace a lost or stolen Nigerian driver's licence
summary: FRSC's official Nigeria Driver's Licence portal issues a Reissue for a licence that is lost, stolen, defaced or illegible. To replace a lost card, first obtain a police extract with particulars of the loss and swear an affidavit. On nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng select DL Application → Reissue of Driver's Licence, not Fresh or Renewal, retrieve the existing record using licence number or NIN and date of birth, complete the application, pay the portal-prescribed class/validity charge and attend any required identity/biometric collection steps.
feeLabel: Reissue fee depends on licence class/term and portal quote
requirements: The existing Driver's Licence number, or registered NIN and date of birth where the portal supports retrieval; this is a reissue of an existing record.
A police extract/report detailing the lost, stolen, damaged or defaced licence.
A sworn affidavit stating the same loss, damage or defacement as required by the FRSC portal.
Correct name, date-of-birth and licence class details, plus legitimate means to pay the charge the official reissue application actually quotes.
Availability to attend a driver licence centre personally if FRSC requires biometric capture or identity verification; the FAQ prohibits sending a proxy for capture.
steps: Report the licence's loss or theft to the police and obtain an extract showing what happened; prepare a court affidavit describing the loss/defacement.
Open https://nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng/ and choose DL Application → Reissue of Driver's Licence. Do not mistakenly start a fresh driving-school-based application.
Retrieve the driver's existing record with the licence number or an available NIN search and the date of birth; resolve a mismatched record with FRSC instead of starting a duplicate identity.
Complete the reissue particulars, choose the applicable licence class/validity and processing centre, and review the generated payment amount before submission.
Pay the prescribed fee using the official channel. Retain the application's receipt, any ID/reference and the portal's biometric/appointment instructions.
Attend the specified FRSC driver licence centre in person if the reissue requires biometric validation or collection checks. A friend cannot substitute their fingerprints or photograph.
Track the application status or contact the identified licence centre, and collect the replacement using the authority's current collection and identification rules.
notes: FRSC's public homepage explicitly requires both police extract and affidavit before a lost/stolen reissue, as well as payment of the prescribed fee.
A renewal is for an expired/expiring licence; a reissue is for an existing licence that is lost, stolen, damaged or illegible. These are separate DL Application choices.
The form can be retrieved using the existing licence number or NIN together with date of birth where supported by FRSC. Do not create a second record to bypass a retrieval problem.
Never use new-licence published prices as an unqualified fixed replacement charge; payment-channel and reissue rules may differ.

title: How to add or remove classes on a Nigerian driver's licence
summary: To add or remove a class on an existing Nigerian driver's licence, FRSC says to use Re-Issue if the licence is still valid or Renewal if expired, then enter the current licence number and select the permitted classes. Its FAQ says multi-class licences can carry up to three classes, while each class may be charged separately. Commercial-licence applications require a capture-centre initiation with medical and driving-school evidence.
feeLabel: Separate licence-class and validity charges; check live FRSC checkout
requirements: The existing driver's licence number and matching date of birth/identity record.
The licence's current expiry date to choose Re-Issue versus Renewal.
The category or classes requested, subject to the maximum of three classes on a multiple-class licence.
For a commercial class, a medical certificate and driving-school certificate, plus attendance at a recognised capture centre.
steps: Check your existing licence validity and identify whether the added class is A/B, a higher class within the same category or a commercial class. FRSC says multi-class licences are limited to three classes.
Open the official Nigeria Driver's Licence portal and choose DL Application → Re-Issue for a valid licence, or DL Application → Renewal after its expiry.
Enter your existing driver's licence number in the requested lookup, then check the identity and existing class information before changing any fields.
Use Processing Centre & Licence Type to select the available classes and 3-year or 5-year validity. The portal applies the allowed class combination rather than permitting every requested class.

summary: NYSC manages requests for relocation through its official electronic process during or after the orientation course. Serving corps members should use their own NYSC portal records, select an eligible ground such as a qualifying marital or health circumstance where applicable, provide the documents required for that ground and await an official NYSC decision.

For health ground: medical report from a Federal or State General Hospital and the doctor's details
steps: Sign in to the official NYSC portal with the serving corps member's details and open the relocation application route when the member is eligible to apply.
Choose the applicable relocation ground and enter the information requested by NYSC; for health or marital grounds, prepare and upload the supporting evidence required for that ground.
Review the supporting documents and request details before submitting the application so the State Coordinator can assess the intended evidence.
After submission, keep checking the NYSC portal for the State Coordinator's recommendation and the final relocation decision because post-camp relocation is processed electronically.
If approved, follow the new posting or relocation instruction shown by NYSC; if unresolved, use the official NYSC channel rather than paying a third party to change the posting.
notes: NYSC states relocation is processed electronically and describes marital and health grounds among concessional cases.
NYSC states that relocations and cancellations are vetted by its responsible offices. Submitting supporting documents is not itself approval to report to another state or employer.

title: What to do if an NYSC discharge certificate is lost
summary: NYSC explicitly does not reprint lost or burnt Certificates of National Service. An ex-corps member instead requests a Letter of Confirmation with a police extract/report, court affidavit, a letter of introduction from the NYSC State Secretariat where the person served and a copy of the original certificate if available. NYSC's published price schedule lists ₦20,000 for loss of a Certificate of National Service/Exemption; confirm payment instructions with the NYSC certification office rather than paying a third party.
feeLabel: NYSC publishes ₦20,000 loss-related charge; no certificate reprint
requirements: A police extract/report documenting the missing Certificate of National Service.
A court affidavit describing the loss and naming the former corps member correctly.
A formal letter of introduction from the NYSC State Secretariat of discharge (the State of Service).
A copy or clear scan of the missing original discharge certificate if one still exists; NYSC says this is optional 'where available'.
Identification/service or call-up details sufficient for NYSC to locate the historical service record; the approving office confirms any extra evidence.
The current verified NYSC certification fee/payment guidance; the published price schedule lists ₦20,000 for certificate loss.
steps: Confirm that the missing document is the Certificate of National Service (discharge certificate). NYSC has separate forms/rules for an Exemption Certificate, and neither is reprinted after loss.
Get a police extract/report describing the lost certificate and obtain a sworn court affidavit about the same incident.
Contact the NYSC State Secretariat where the former corps member was discharged and obtain the required Letter of Introduction from that State of Service.
Attach a copy of the original certificate when available, and prepare identity/service evidence to match the NYSC record. Do not invent a certificate number if no copy exists.
Present the complete request to the official NYSC certification channel identified by the State Secretariat and request a Letter of Confirmation, not a replacement original.
Verify the applicable fee directly with NYSC before paying: its published schedule lists ₦20,000 for loss of Certificate of National Service or Exemption. Retain an official receipt/reference.

Use the NYSC certification office's reference or written response to check the request's progress. If approved, NYSC issues a Letter of Confirmation, not another Certificate of National Service. The public certification instructions do not promise a fixed date for completion.
notes: NYSC states as a matter of policy that a lost or burnt Certificate of National Service is not reprinted and a Letter of Confirmation is issued instead.
The required introduction must come from the State of Service where the ex-corps member was discharged; a former employer's casual note is not established as an equivalent.
A copy of the lost certificate is requested only when available; losing that copy does not negate the requirement for independent police, affidavit and service-state records.

NYSC publishes a ₦20,000 loss-related charge in its official fee schedule (last updated 19 August 2024). Payment/processing methods require direct confirmation, and intermediaries should not receive personal-account transfers.
NYSC does not issue Certificates of National Service by proxy under its certification policy. Seek official clarification about Letter of Confirmation collection requirements.

title: NPC Birth Attestation Nigeria: Eligibility, USD 80 Fee and Download
summary: Adults aged 18 or older can request a birth attestation through the National Population Commission (NPC) self-service portal. The earlier NPC self-service fee notice listed a non-refundable USD 80 convenience fee, requires a court-sworn affidavit and identity checks, and allows a certificate download after a successful application. Applicants without a NIN can receive a temporary Birth ID for NIMC enrolment; children aged 0–17 use birth registration instead.
feeLabel: Previously listed USD 80 online fee; reconfirm with NPC
requirements: Applicant must be aged 18 or above; children aged 0–17 belong in NPC birth registration, not adult birth attestation.
A court-sworn affidavit, a valid email address and an active mobile phone number.
An NIN for mandatory verification if one is available. NPC offers a temporary attestation/Birth ID route for an applicant without an NIN, followed by a visit to NIMC for enrolment.
Registration state, current local government area and a preferred registration centre, as requested by the portal.

A stable internet connection and good lighting for portal face capture when available. NPC's earlier online flow listed a USD 80 non-refundable convenience charge, but its availability and current price must be reconfirmed on the official service.
steps: Open the National Population Commission's official website and choose Services → Birth Attestation. The formerly published direct attestation subdomain failed the current link check; if the service is unavailable, use NPC's official FAQs/contact details or ask an authorised office how to proceed. Adults aged 18+ use attestation rather than children's birth registration.
Prepare your court-sworn affidavit, contact details and accurate birth information. Make sure your name and date of birth are consistent with the identity records you intend to use.

If you have an NIN, complete the portal's mandatory NIN verification before proceeding. If you do not have one, follow NPC's temporary attestation/Birth ID option and its instruction to enrol with NIMC; do not enter another person's NIN.
Supply the registration state, current LGA and nearest available registration centre requested in the form. Complete the face capture with stable internet, clear lighting and a plain background.

Review every field before submitting: NPC warns that an applicant can make only one attestation application. If the portal asks you to amend a date of birth after NIN validation, follow its stated restrictions rather than guessing or repeatedly submitting.

Only after the official NPC application service is available, verify the payment amount displayed inside its legitimate flow. The earlier fee notice listed a USD 80 non-refundable convenience charge; save the payment reference emailed by NPC and do not pay an unofficial intermediary.

Use the portal's Check Status or payment-reference option after processing. NPC says certificates can be downloaded once after a successful application; use its reprint route if you need another copy rather than starting a duplicate attestation.
notes: On 15 October 2026, the earlier direct birth-attestation service address did not resolve during website link validation. Use NPC's main website and its Services directory or official contact channels. Do not treat an old direct portal link as proof that the application is currently accepting submissions.

The two services cover different ages: NPC attestation is for people aged 18 and above, whereas child birth registration covers ages 0–17. An online convenience charge for one route must not be presented as the price of all NPC birth services.

The temporary Birth ID issued to applicants without a NIN is not a replacement for an NIN. NPC says it is used during subsequent NIMC enrolment and cannot be validated as an NIN on NIMC's modification portal.

If Check Status says “No Record Found”, NPC says that function works after the attestation process has been successfully completed. Use your original payment reference or the portal's resume option before considering another payment.

NPC allows a single certificate download after success, with a separate reprint option for additional copies. Keep the payment reference private and use official NPC support if approval or retrieval does not work.

A functional email address for the payment reference, updates and application status.

Enter the holder's correct identity and certificate data and supply the NIN when available. The portal describes a temporary certificate number for applicants without NIN.
Upload the non-digital certificate image and, if applying for attestation reissuance, add the court affidavit NPC specifies.
Review the application and non-refundable payment before completing the official checkout; keep the emailed payment reference.
Use Check Status or Update Application to monitor a pending request instead of paying and starting a duplicate submission.
After approval, plan a secure download/print immediately because NPC warns that the new certificate can only be downloaded once.

Read the displayed US$30 reprint charge before choosing the correct certificate type from the portal selector.
Enter the existing registered person and certificate record details in the fields shown by NPC, checking spelling and birth date carefully.
Review any matched record before making the official reprint payment; do not register a fresh birth merely to replace an old certificate.

Do not share a scanned certificate with an unofficial agent offering a shortcut.

title: How to reset a JAMB profile password

Send PASSWORD, one space and the email address on the JAMB profile to 55019 or 66019 from that same SIM; do not confuse it with RESEND for profile code retrieval. Sign in only through JAMB's official e-Facility after receiving its reply.

Exact email address originally associated with the JAMB e-Facility profile.

Open SMS on that same number and type PASSWORD followed by a space and the registered email, for example PASSWORD candidate@example.com.
Send the SMS to either 55019 or 66019 and read the response delivered to the linked number; allow for SMS service charges.
Use the reset credential or instruction JAMB returns to sign in at the official e-Facility profile rather than a website sent by a third party.

summary: FCT-IRS lets recipients verify a Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) electronically using its dedicated fcttaxportal.fctirs.gov.ng/tccver.aspx form or the QR code on the certificate. The form explicitly asks for the TCC reference, taxpayer TIN, verifier's email and organisation/individual name; compare the official response with the actual paper/PDF certificate before accepting it.
requirements: The TCC reference number printed on the certificate being checked.
The taxpayer's TIN that appears on or is tied to the same tax-clearance document.
An email address to receive the system's acknowledgement and the verifier's organisation or individual name.
The original physical or PDF TCC for comparing the verification response.
steps: Open FCT-IRS's official Verify TCC service from https://fctirs.gov.ng/ or navigate directly to https://fcttaxportal.fctirs.gov.ng/tccver.aspx and use the verification form.
If starting from a printed certificate, scan its QR code and confirm the destination is an FCT-IRS-controlled verification site before entering personal information.
Enter the certificate's TCC Ref# and the associated taxpayer TIN in the exact form fields.
Supply the verifier email and Name of Organization/Individual as requested and submit the official online check.
Compare the electronic verification details with the certificate presented, including identity, reference and status; FCT-IRS requires the verified and physical TCC to match.
If the portal fails or the numbers conflict, contact FCT-IRS through its published enquiry route before relying on the document or paying any additional demand.
notes: The FCT-IRS dedicated TCC verification page and QR scan are verification tools, not a fresh TCC application.
Do not confuse the issuing year's certificate validity with the timing of a verification response.
FCT-IRS also accepts correspondence for authenticity checks, but its current public verification form is a distinct online service.
A missing or mismatched TCC result is a reason to seek confirmation from FCT-IRS, not immediate proof of forgery.

title: How to register or verify a Tax ID from Edo State
summary: Edo State Internal Revenue Service's December 2025 guidance offers three concrete Tax Identification Number (TIN) routes: the official Joint Tax Board portal tin.jtb.gov.ng for registration/verification, the *668# USSD route, and decentralised EIRS zonal offices. Edo IRS announced fourteen additional state registration centres; its ERAS site remains a separate state revenue-account portal, not the only way to obtain or confirm a TIN.
requirements: For an individual, the genuine taxpayer identity/NIN data accepted by the JTB Tax ID system.
For a company, CAC/business registration details matching the taxpayer entity being registered or verified.
A mobile SIM able to use *668# USSD if selecting the SMS-independent phone route.
A location/official EIRS contact when face-to-face registration is preferable.
steps: Decide whether you need a first Tax ID registration or to verify an already-issued TIN; do not create a duplicate registration if the taxpayer already has a number.
Open https://tin.jtb.gov.ng, the specific Tax ID registration/verification URL published by Edo IRS, and select the individual or corporate category shown.
If an internet form is not practical, dial *668# from a supported Nigerian phone and use the Tax ID menu published in EIRS's official announcement.
For an in-person option, visit an EIRS zonal office: the notice identifies Oredo 1 at 18 Ihama Road, GRA Benin City and Egor at 190 Uselu-Lagos Road among fourteen additional centres.
Provide the correct individual NIN or CAC business details requested for the taxpayer, and check spelling/registration identity before submission.
Keep the generated Tax ID/verification record and verify it through the official JTB route rather than using ERAS login status as proof of Tax ID issuance.
If a taxpayer identity cannot be matched, contact EIRS at info@eirs.gov.ng or 0813 097 0146 from the public notice for authoritative next steps.
notes: EIRS's 4 December 2025 official notice expressly announces *668# and tin.jtb.gov.ng; the original guide did not provide either starting action.
EIRS lists fourteen additional registration points across the state; verify opening hours with the selected office rather than assuming it accepts walk-ins on any day.
The JTB Tax ID system and Edo ERAS revenue dashboard have different functions. One can be used for Tax ID lookup while the other handles state revenue services.
Never enter taxpayer NIN/CAC details into a third-party 'TIN generator' website.

title: Anambra ASIN Registration: Create, Find or Recover Your Identity Number
summary: Apply for the Anambra State Identity Number (ASIN) from the official AIRS enumeration page by choosing Individual, Informal/Enterprise or Corporate. Already registered? Search for your existing ASIN using the state’s separate lookup service; do not create another number. ASIN is not the same as your federal NIN or a tax-payment receipt.
feeLabel: Check official enrolment requirements; no confirmed online fee quoted
requirements: Know which category applies: Individual (personal registration), Informal/Enterprise (informal business or sole-enterprise enumeration) or Corporate (registered organisation). Each category has different fields and supporting requirements.
Correct personal or business identification and contact information for the chosen form; the portal may request a NIN for an individual, but your NIN is not the state ASIN itself.
A working mobile number or email to receive the form's confirmation and manage future state transactions.
If you believe you already have an ASIN, the original mobile number, email, NIN or ASIN for the official search before attempting a new enumeration.
For later Anambra state tax or permit payment, the particular MDA or invoice/payment reference; these payment details are separate from the act of creating your ASIN.
steps: Open the Anambra State Internal Revenue Service official enumeration site at https://tax.services.an.gov.ng/create-asin. Check the AIRS/Anambra government domain before typing personal identification; avoid sponsored lookalike forms.

Choose the form that actually matches you: Individual, Informal/Enterprise or Corporate. Do not choose Corporate for a personal identity or assume an existing business's ASIN covers every individual who works there.

Enter the requested details as they appear on the identification or registration records used for that category. The official form controls which information is required; confirm each spelling, phone number and email before submitting.

Submit the completed enumeration and securely save the number or acknowledgement actually issued by AIRS. ASIN is designed as a unique one-time identifier, not something to regenerate whenever you pay tax or apply for another state service.

If you previously registered, use https://tax.services.an.gov.ng/asin/search instead of the new-enumeration link. The Anambra government payment directory says the lookup accepts phone number, NIN, email or ASIN; recover the existing number before opening another identity record.

Already have an ASIN but cannot log in? The separate taxpayer login at https://tax.services.an.gov.ng/auth/login accepts Email / ASIN with your password and provides a Forgot password route. Do not use the registration form for password recovery.

To pay a tax, levy or official invoice, start from the Anambra government's Where to Pay directory and use its agency payment channel. ASIN identifies the taxpayer or applicant; the payment receipt has its own verification page. ASIN creation, payment, login and receipt verification are not interchangeable tasks.

If the form repeatedly fails, your details conflict, or the ASIN cannot be found, use the government service listing to reach AIRS (07066727750) and request a record check or correction. Take existing acknowledgement and identification evidence to an official service desk only if the authority instructs you, not an unverified agent.
notes: The Anambra State Government says an ASIN is a one-time unique identifier for individuals and businesses using its public services. It is often needed before an Anambra government payment or state permit application, but is distinct from CAC business registration and the federal NIN.

The registration portal distinguishes Individual, Informal/Enterprise and Corporate applicants. Using the incorrect category can create mismatched records for later payments, business permissions or tax obligations; choose the route applicable to the actual person or entity.

AIRS has a separate existing-ASIN lookup. The state service directory lists phone number, NIN, email or ASIN as search options. Finding a previously issued number is not the same operation as creating a new ASIN account.

An ASIN can be used for other official Anambra systems, including payment and building permit transactions; those systems may require separate registration, documents, fees or approvals. An ASIN alone is not a business licence or evidence a tax has been paid.

The taxpayer login takes Email / ASIN and password, with password recovery. The state's receipt/certificate verification portal is also separate, so do not misread a verified payment receipt as proof a new ASIN is generated.

The currently available official online service directory does not list a universal ASIN registration price or guaranteed process duration. Older state-issued procedural PDFs mention free ASIN enrolment assistance and an approximately ten-minute process, but an historical administrative estimate should not be advertised as a live guarantee.

For a missing, duplicated or inconsistent identity record, the state services entry lists AIRS telephone 07066727750. Present exact reference and category details through official channels only; never disclose passwords, one-time codes or sensitive identity data to third parties offering paid ASIN creation.

The source pages linked below are managed by the responsible state entities. MyNigeriaGuide is an independent information service and does not accept ASIN applications, store your NIN or process state fees.

requirements: Name details
One of the identity/contact options accepted by the portal, such as NIN, BVN or phone number, as applicable
A real NIN, BVN or phone contact accepted by the portal, plus the matching legal given/surname details.

notes: Lagos State Revenue Portal's live Create Payer ID form accepts NIN, BVN and Phone as separate search criteria.

An existing identity match should be recovered, not duplicated to solve a forgotten password.

title: What to do if your Nigerian passport is lost
summary: If a Nigerian passport is lost or stolen, NIS directs the holder to Apply for Renewal/Re-issue on the official passport portal, not to submit a new first-time application. Required evidence includes an NPC birth certificate or qualifying court declaration, Local Government Indigeneship Certificate, police extract describing the loss and a High Court sworn affidavit. Dual nationals holding a foreign passport should also upload its data page. Pay the actual NIS replacement charge, save receipt/acknowledgement and attend the selected passport office for biometric capture.
feeLabel: NIS replacement fees apply; confirm total at the official checkout
requirements: Existing passport number or other records identifying the lost document, where available; report details truthfully rather than guessing.
Birth certificate from the National Population Commission or a qualifying declaration of age from a Federal/State High Court or Customary Court of Appeal.
Local Government Certificate of Indigeneship, consistent with the applicant's identity and nationality record.
Police extract recording loss of the passport and a sworn High Court affidavit specifically for the loss.
The data page of a valid non-Nigerian passport if the holder has dual nationality; relevant marriage or other civil evidence where the applicant's names differ.
Official passport-portal access, payment method, selection of a processing centre and ability to attend in person with original identity evidence.
steps: Obtain the police extract/report for the lost passport and a sworn High Court affidavit explaining the loss, including the original passport identity details you can reliably confirm.
Gather NPC birth record or qualifying declaration of age, local-government indigeneship evidence, and any relevant foreign passport data page or name-change record when applicable.

Open https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and select Apply for Renewal/Re-issue Passport. NIS's official lost-passport guide explicitly uses this existing-passport route, not the Fresh Passport pathway.
Enter the actual identity/passport details requested, select the appropriate processing centre, and upload the police extract, affidavit, citizenship/birth and other category documents.
Check the final amount shown by NIS for this replacement, pay through the official portal and print/save the actual payment and application acknowledgement slips.
Attend the processing/biometric appointment in person with original records the office requests. If applying from outside Nigeria, consult the Nigerian mission responsible for that processing route.

Check the application status through the NIS portal and the selected office's collection directions. If the missing booklet is found later, do not resume using a passport already formally declared lost; ask NIS how to surrender or handle it.
notes: NIS warns the continued use of a passport already declared lost can be treated as fraudulent misuse of a government document. A recovered booklet should be taken to NIS rather than reused without clearance.
Dual nationals with a foreign passport must disclose and upload its data page under the official NIS loss application instructions.
Different personal-data changes or ordinary validity renewals use different evidence rules; the loss affidavit and police report are not substitutes for a name/date correction application.
An online form or a receipt does not eliminate the physical identity and biometric checks required for reissue.

title: How to reissue a lost, damaged or stolen NIN slip
summary: NIMC publishes conflicting figures for NIN slip reissuance on two official pages. The dedicated current Fees table says ₦600 for loss, damage or theft and ₦1,000 for each modified data field, while its detailed reissuance page still says ₦500. For loss/theft, NIMC requests a recent police report, affidavit and photo ID; damage needs the damaged slip; post-modification reissue needs the transaction slip. Check the generated NIMC/Remita invoice instead of guessing.
feeLabel: Official fee pages conflict: ₦600/₦1,000 vs older ₦500
feeNote: NIMC's Fees table states ₦600 for loss/damage/theft and ₦1,000 per modified field, but its NIN Slip Re-Issuance instructions still cite ₦500. Both pages are published by NIMC. Confirm the exact selected service and generated official Remita invoice; do not tell users that the discrepancy is resolved or that an old ₦500 figure is necessarily payable.
requirements: Loss or theft: a recent police extract/report, court affidavit for the missing document and photo identification.
Damage: the original damaged NIN slip to present for replacement.
Reissue after modification: the original NIMC transaction slip from the already-approved data correction.
An official NIMC payment invoice and Remita Retrieval Reference (RRR) for the applicable reissue item.
steps: Determine whether the slip is lost, stolen, damaged or being reissued after an approved data modification; collect the separate evidence NIMC specifies for that reason.
Read both NIMC's current Fees table and its older detailed Re-Issuance instructions so you understand the ₦600/₦1,000 versus ₦500 published discrepancy.
At remita.net choose the National Identity Management Commission as biller, select the exact reissue purpose and generate an official invoice/RRR.

Review the amount that NIMC/Remita generates before paying. If the discrepancy persists or the requested purpose is missing, confirm it with NIMC rather than choosing an unrelated fee to force payment.
Pay using the supported card, bank, USSD, internet-banking or wallet option, keeping the actual official payment reference.
Present the required police report/affidavit/ID, damaged slip or modification transaction slip as relevant, along with payment evidence, through the NIMC authorised reissue route.
Receive and inspect the reissued slip; if a downloaded/printed version is provided, ensure the recorded NIN and the corrected fields are consistent.
notes: The NIN itself is not being replaced; this service issues another copy of the slip.
This page must remain explicit about the official-source fee conflict instead of changing both figures into a false definitive price.
Date-of-birth data correction fees are unrelated to the fee for reissuing a slip after modification.
NIMC's detailed page describes an 'Immediately' target, which should not be treated as a guaranteed same-day completion across every route.

title: How to change your name on NIN
summary: To correct an eligible name field on an existing NIN, use NIMC's official Self-Service Modifications portal or its published centre-assisted route, not a new NIN enrolment. NIMC lists a sworn affidavit and newspaper extract for a name change, plus a marriage certificate when the change is due to marriage. Confirm the fee on the actual modification invoice before payment.
feeNote: NIMC's published fees table lists ₦2,000 per ordinary updatable field and separately prices date-of-birth corrections. Provider instructions can differ across NIMC pages and payment routes, so the live official invoice and the precise requested name fields determine what is payable. Do not infer a DOB charge for a name-only modification.
requirements: Your existing valid NIN and access to the NIMC self-service account or the authorised NIMC centre process.
Sworn affidavit and newspaper extract supporting the requested name change.
Marriage certificate where the change is due to marriage.
Other identity or civil records requested by NIMC to reconcile the name with the existing identity record.
steps: Start from nimc.gov.ng/self-service-modifications/ and follow NIMC's genuine self-service modification link. Do not submit a fresh NIN enrolment.
Sign in and choose the specific name field(s) to modify; check the present NIN entry and the spelling on your supporting documents.
Prepare the affidavit and newspaper extract, and add marriage evidence where applicable. Upload only the documents required for the selected request.
Check NIMC's current fee table and the official invoice for the selected fields, then complete payment only inside the provider-authorised route.
Review the corrected spelling and submit; retain the official transaction acknowledgement.

Check the official application status. If self-service is unsuitable, ask a NIMC enrolment centre for its assisted document-verification process; an informational NIMC page is not itself a completed application.
notes: An existing NIN remains the starting point: a name change does not justify creating a second identity record.
NIMC distinguishes its self-service portal from centre-assisted modification; do not label all name changes exclusively online or exclusively walk-in.
Affidavit, newspaper extract and marriage certificate requirements are conditional on the reason for the change. Ensure submitted documents genuinely support the requested spelling.
NIMC's ₦2,000 listing relates to ordinary updatable fields; date of birth has a separate tariff and should not be bundled into a name-only fee.

title: How to change your phone number on NIN
summary: Change a NIN-linked phone number through NIMC's official modification workflow. The old registered SIM may be needed to access a device-bound account; NIMC's guidance requires a police report in a lost/damaged-number case. Ordinary updatable-field fees are currently listed at ₦2,000, subject to the real portal invoice.
requirements: Police report for the lost/damaged-phone-number modification case
Existing NIN and access to the NIMC self-service modification account
The new Nigerian phone number entered in +234 format without the leading zero
Evidence explaining loss or damage of the previous number, including the police report specified for that case.
A replacement line the applicant controls, entered in +234 international format without the leading domestic zero.
steps: Check whether the old phone number is merely inactive or actually lost/stolen. If it is recoverable, confirm legitimate SIM replacement with the network before changing sensitive identity details.

Open the NIMC official self-service modifications entry point with the applicant's NIN. A previously registered browser/device may be needed; follow NIMC's authorised unlink procedure if access fails.
Select the Phone Number modification, not the Date of Birth or NIN re-enrolment service.
For a lost or damaged number, prepare the police report called for by NIMC and upload the documentary evidence the current form requests.
Enter the new number using +234 without the leading zero; inspect each digit and ensure it belongs to the NIN holder.
Compare the on-screen payment against the official NIMC fees table, complete the authorised charge and retain the transaction reference.
Submit and monitor the request until it is approved. Confirm that the updated record reflects the new number before relying on it for other agency services.
If the request remains blocked by an old device or identity mismatch, contact NIMC modification support; do not give an agent your NIN account password or OTP.
notes: NIMC currently lists ₦2,000 for an ordinary updatable field, excluding the separate date-of-birth fee.
The official phone-change guidance asks for a police report in the lost/damaged-number case; document requirements for other circumstances may differ.
NIMC's self-service account can be bound to the device/browser used for registration. Repeatedly opening new accounts may not resolve this.

title: How to change your address on NIN
summary: NIMC lists address as an updatable NIN detail. To change it, start with NIMC's official Self-Service Modifications route and provide current evidence such as a utility bill, tenancy agreement, bank statement or community-leader attestation. An assisted NIMC enrolment-centre route is also published; confirm the actual payment invoice and do not create a second NIN.
requirements: Existing NIN and access to the official NIMC self-service modification account or an authorised NIMC centre.
The complete new address as it should appear on the identity record.
Supporting proof of address accepted by NIMC: utility bill, tenancy agreement, bank statement or community-leader attestation.
An official invoice or application acknowledgement for the selected address field.
steps: Open the self-service modifications section on nimc.gov.ng and follow NIMC's official link to its modification system.
Sign in with the existing NIN and select Address as the specific field to change.
Enter the new address exactly as supported by the available evidence, then upload the relevant utility bill, tenancy agreement, bank statement or attestation accepted by NIMC.
Review the requested field and charge against the official NIMC fee schedule and live invoice before paying.
Submit the modification and keep the official reference or receipt to check the result.
If self-service cannot handle the case, contact a NIMC enrolment centre for the published assisted procedure and identity-document checks.
notes: NIMC's adult modifications page lists four types of address evidence, including bank statements; the earlier guide omitted that option.
An address correction does not change the NIN itself; do not apply for a replacement number.
NIMC's public fee table lists ₦2,000 for an ordinary updatable field, while the actual charge should be confirmed on the official invoice.
Do not assume the document will be accepted if the new address and supporting record are inconsistent.

title: How to lodge a complaint about a withheld or held WAEC result
summary: Candidates whose WAEC results are marked withheld or held can use the complaints/defence portal linked from WAEC Nigeria's official announcement. Start at WAEC's notice, follow its waecinternational.org complaints link, identify the correct examination and submit a factual account. This is a complaint channel, not a guarantee that WAEC will release a withheld result. The complaints/defence channel is for candidates whose published result is held or withheld. WAEC review, result-score protests and certificate corrections are separate processes with different eligibility.
feeLabel: No complaint fee stated on WAEC's notice
requirements: The candidate's examination year, type and examination/candidate number needed to identify the held or withheld record.
The wording/status shown on the affected result and an accurate account of the complaint or defence.

The result notice showing the held or withheld status, plus any examination-day incident report, correction letter or WAEC correspondence that supports the candidate's account. Supply contact information in the current complaints form.
steps: Open the official WAEC Nigeria notice headed 'Complaint Portal for Candidates Whose Results Were Withheld/Held' and follow its link to waecinternational.org/complaints.
Record the exact wording displayed on the candidate's result: held, withheld, cancelled or partial release are not necessarily handled by identical routes.
Check that you are entering the WAEC complaints domain linked by the official notice rather than a lookalike form or a social-media message.
Select or identify the affected examination/candidate according to the current form and provide the explanation or defence requested.
Submit only facts and relevant supporting documents. Save the official acknowledgement or reference if one is issued.
For school candidates, inform the school principal as WAEC's FAQ normally routes school-candidate communication through principals; retain copies of the school examination record.
If an official acknowledgement is not produced, record the date and legitimate portal reference and seek WAEC support rather than paying anyone to release a result.

title: How to enrol for a BVN in Nigeria
summary: BVN registration within Nigeria is free and now restricted to people aged 18 or older under the CBN rules effective 1 May 2026. The applicant must use an authorised bank enrolment location, present permitted identity evidence and attend personal biometric capture. An acknowledgement is not the assigned BVN; follow up using the enrolment reference if it is delayed.
feeNote: CBN has stated that BVN registration within Nigeria is free. Do not pay an unofficial enrolment fee.
timeline: NIBSS says a BVN can be obtained within 72 hours after enrolment once the enrolment data has synchronised with the central database.
requirements: Applicant must be at least 18 years old under the CBN amendment effective 1 May 2026
A valid means of identification accepted by the enrolling bank or authorised channel
Personal attendance for facial image, fingerprints and other biometric capture
A working phone number for enrolment communication and later BVN-related services
Applicant's own valid identity record and ability to appear for live biometric capture, not a proxy enrolment.
A phone number controlled by the applicant, reviewed carefully before submission because CBN limits changes to BVN-linked phone numbers.
steps: Check CBN's BVN eligibility notice before travelling: only people aged 18 or above may obtain a new BVN, and enrolment inside Nigeria is free.
Choose a bank branch or authorised BVN enrolment channel and confirm that the location performs BVN enrolment before travelling there.
Take the valid identification accepted by the enrolling institution, complete the BVN enrolment form and check the demographic details before biometric capture begins.
Present yourself for the required biometric capture, including facial image and fingerprints, and make sure the enrolment operator completes the submission rather than leaving it as a draft.
Collect and keep the acknowledgement slip or transaction ID issued after enrolment because it is the reference to use if the BVN does not arrive as expected.

Wait for NIBSS to synchronise the enrolment data and generate the BVN; once the enrolling institution or BVN notification provides the number, give it to each bank where it needs to be linked to your accounts. If it is still unavailable after 72 hours, follow up with the enrolling institution using the transaction ID.
Ask the bank's BVN desk to confirm its accepted photo identity document and the branch's biometric service hours; bring the original document, not a photo of another person's ID.
Check that the name, date of birth and phone number entered by the operator exactly match the supporting identity record before submitting the fingerprint and face capture.
Do not enter your BVN into a 'free BVN generation' website: a BVN is assigned through enrolment and its number must remain linked to the same person.
If the registered phone number needs a later update, ask the bank about the May 2026 rule permitting a BVN-linked phone number change only once; preserve the correct line from the start.
notes: CBN says BVN enrolment in Nigeria is free.
From 1 May 2026, CBN says only people aged 18 and above may enrol for BVN.
CBN's 2026 amendment also states that a BVN-linked phone number may be changed only once.
CBN's 2026 reforms impose a minimum age of 18 for BVN enrolment and allow only one change of the linked mobile number.
The enrolling bank remains the first point of contact for a BVN record or unresolved synchronisation issue, even if the NIBSS database generates the final number.

Use the mobile phone number that was registered during BVN enrolment; the retrieval service will not return the BVN from an unrelated number.
Allow the ₦20 service charge and read the BVN returned on screen carefully, then store it somewhere private rather than sharing it publicly.

If the registered number is no longer available or the lookup cannot resolve the record, contact your bank or the institution that manages the BVN record rather than repeatedly paying the USSD charge.
Read the returned eleven-digit number privately and compare it with any BVN confirmation previously issued by the enrolling bank; do not post it on a group chat or supply it to a reversal agent.

notes: A BVN is not a bank account number or a payment credential, but it is sensitive identity information and should still be protected.
NIBSS requires the phone number registered to the BVN for *565*0# retrieval.
NIBSS currently lists *565*0# for BVN retrieval from the phone number registered to the BVN and publishes a ₦20 service fee.
