title: How to register as a taxpayer with Ogun State IRS
summary: Get an Ogun State S-TIN through the Ogun State Internal Revenue Service's current individual or organisation registration workflow. The live self-service FAQ says individuals search using a phone number, while corporate applicants search using a CAC number; an existing taxpayer should recover their S-TIN rather than register again.
feeNote: Use the official Ogun State IRS taxpayer registration route and approved revenue channels.
timeline: Account access depends on registration details being accepted by Ogun State IRS.
requirements: Individual or organisation identity information appropriate to the taxpayer type
Contact and address information used by Ogun State IRS to create the taxpayer record
For organisations, legal registration details and employer/tax-agent information where applicable
For individual registration, a usable phone number and correct personal/contact and local-government address details.
For incorporated entities, the CAC registration number and legal organisation details as required by Ogun's corporate route.
An accessible email for the registration activation/password link, or an official revenue-office update if existing data lacks a contact email.
steps: Open https://www.ogunstaterevenue.com/en/selfservice, then under Get Ogun State Tax ID Number select Individual or Organization. This is the official Ogun IRS S-TIN entry point.
Before creating a new registration, use the search function: individuals search by phone number and corporations search by CAC number, according to Ogun's own FAQ.
If the taxpayer exists, retrieve the existing S-TIN or use Get Access Password rather than creating a duplicate state tax identity.
If no record exists, select Register, provide legal name, email, telephone, address and the registration type's other required fields.
Submit and monitor the registered email for the activation link and instructions to create the access password.
Sign in with the S-TIN/phone/email and password through the official Self Service Portal; review the taxpayer's identity and contact details.
If Get Password fails because the profile has incomplete contact records, visit an Ogun Revenue Office or use its official registration-update support process.
Once active, use the separate state tax return, payment and TCC actions appropriate to the taxpayer; successful registration does not prove tax was paid.
notes: Ogun IRS calls its state identifier S-TIN and distinguishes individual-phone from corporate-CAC search.
The official Self Service FAQ says incomplete registration may prevent sending the activation/password link and describes a revenue-office correction path.
Ogun's older login pages use legacy terminology, so start from the current Self Service Centre rather than assuming every historic login route is interchangeable.

title: How to obtain and verify an Ogun State eTCC
summary: The Ogun State IRS process for a Tax Clearance Certificate, including the preceding tax record, employee/self-employed evidence and online certificate verification.
feeNote: Ogun State IRS states that there is no processing fee for obtaining an eTCC. Tax liabilities themselves must still be settled.
timeline: Ogun State IRS says an eTCC can be obtained within about 72 hours after payment and proper filing of all required documents.
requirements: An Ogun State taxpayer/S-TIN record
Evidence that the relevant personal income tax obligations for the preceding years have been paid or properly assessed
For a self-employed applicant, receipts and income/tax records for the three years preceding the application year
For an employee, employer income and tax-remittance evidence for the preceding three years
Any additional document requested by the Ogun State assessment authority
steps: Check the taxpayer's Ogun State registration and payment history and resolve missing tax payments before requesting the certificate.
If self-employed, submit the eTCC request to the relevant assessment authority with the preceding three-year payment evidence.
If employed, have the employer provide the income and tax-remittance information needed for the assessment authority to confirm the preceding years.
Wait for the Ogun State assessment authority to review the records and notify you when the eTCC is ready.
Use the official Ogun State TCC verification page with the TCC number and S-TIN when the certificate needs to be independently checked.
notes: Ogun State IRS says the eTCC covers the three years preceding the year of application and is renewed annually.
The published FAQ says eTCC processing itself is free; that does not remove any unpaid tax liability that must be settled.
Use the current state portal when verifying a certificate rather than relying only on the printed copy.

title: How to get a Rivers State RIVTIN
summary: Register or recover a Rivers State RIVTIN through RIVTAMIS, the Rivers State Internal Revenue Service's taxpayer system. Search for an existing individual or corporate account before creating a new one, then validate the registered contact information and use the issued Tax ID for separate payment, returns or TCC services.
feeNote: Use the official Rivers RIVTAMIS platform for account registration and RIVTIN activation.
timeline: Rivers State IRS says account activation takes about 24 hours after registration.
requirements: Individual or corporate identity information used to search for an existing taxpayer record before creating a new one
A valid email address and phone number for account access and activation
For organisations, the registered organisation name and corporate information required by RIVTAMIS
Individual or organisation identification and contact information; corporate users must follow the organisation registration class.
A valid email/phone to receive any required activation or account-recovery instructions.
steps: Open the official Rivers RIVTAMIS website and look for Search RivTIN before registering. Search an existing taxpayer first.
If a matching RIVTIN is already assigned to the individual or organisation, use the recovery/sign-in process rather than creating duplicate accounts.
If new, choose the Individual or Corporate Sign Up route that matches the entity type.
Complete the true legal name, tax identity, phone, email and address/organisation fields requested by the official form.
Confirm the submission and complete any email or phone activation steps; keep the taxpayer reference without publishing it.
If activation is delayed, use the official RIVTAMIS status/contact route rather than inventing a 24-hour guaranteed completion time.
Sign in using the registered email or Tax ID when the account is active and verify the information returned.
Use the RIVTIN for the separate Demand Notice Payment, TCC verification, filing or other state tax function; registration alone does not issue tax clearance.
notes: RIVTAMIS has a public Search RivTIN lookup and separate sign-in for Email/TAXID.
The original Rivers guide quotes about 24 hours for activation, but this is an agency indication rather than guaranteed account activation for every application.
Do not substitute a Lagos Payer ID or federal NRS Tax ID for Rivers' internal account access unless the official form explicitly accepts it.

sources.label: Agency source for process, eligibility and exception handling

title: How to apply for and verify a Rivers State Tax Clearance Certificate
summary: How individuals and organisations use RIVTAMIS for direct assessment or corporate TCC requests, track the application and verify a Rivers State certificate.
feeLabel: Tax liability depends on the assessment
feeNote: Rivers State IRS does not publish one universal TCC amount; the taxpayer must settle the assessment and use the official RIVTAMIS payment process.
timeline: Processing depends on registration, assessment, payment and review; RIVTAMIS provides request tracking after submission.
requirements: An active RIVTIN linked to the taxpayer's RIVTAMIS account
A complete taxpayer or company profile with a valid email address and phone number
For direct assessment, the relevant invoice/payment information and supporting PDF documents
For a corporate request, approved annual returns and an updated employee list before generating staff TCCs
steps: Sign in to RIVTAMIS with the taxpayer's email, phone number or RIVTIN/TAXID and confirm that the profile is complete.
For an individual using Direct Assessment, open TCC > Direct Assessment, select the tax year and tax station, and enter the required payment or assessment information.
Upload the supporting documents and payment receipt in the format accepted by RIVTAMIS, then submit the TCC request.
For a corporate TCC request, confirm that annual returns are approved, open TCC Requests, select the year and employee type, and generate the certificate request for the relevant staff.
Track the request from the TCC history or tracking area until the certificate is issued.
When checking an existing certificate, use RIVTAMIS TCC Verification and compare the result with the certificate presented.
notes: Rivers State IRS says Direct Assessment is the route used by an individual taxpayer to declare income and process personal tax obligations directly.
Corporate TCC requests depend on the organisation's annual returns, profile and employee records being complete.
RIVTAMIS provides a separate public verification function, so a third party can check a TCC instead of relying only on a paper copy.
For a company or PAYE employer, sign in with the corporate RIVTAMIS account and use the TCC Requests menu after the organisation's annual returns and employee records are complete.

title: How to add, remove or change a company director with CAC
summary: Use CAC post-incorporation filing to record an actual appointment, cessation or change of director particulars after the company has made the required corporate decision. A CAC director change does not automatically update share ownership or the Persons with Significant Control register.
feeNote: Use the current CAC fee schedule and the amount generated by iCRP for the exact director filing. Late filings can attract additional charges.
timeline: CAC's current service timeline lists 12 working hours for CAC 7/director particulars and Edit Director filings after receipt of the required documents or resolution of a query.
requirements: The company's CAC registration number and access to an iCRP account authorised to make its post-incorporation filings
The corporate resolution or approval supporting the appointment, removal or change
Identity and statutory particulars of the incoming or affected director
The consent, notice or supporting corporate document applicable to the exact director change
Accurate effective date, appointment/cessation reason and affected director's identity particulars; signed consent or notice if required by the selected filing.
steps: Decide whether this is a new appointment, removal/cessation or correction of existing particulars; obtain the company authorisation before editing an official public record.
Sign in to CAC iCRP with the account authorised to manage post-incorporation filings for the company.
Open the company's post-incorporation services and select the director appointment, removal or particulars-change transaction that matches the approved corporate action.
Enter the affected director's statutory particulars and upload the corporate resolution, identity and consent or notice documents applicable to the filing.
Review the director information, generate the official CAC transaction and pay the filing or late fee shown by iCRP.
From the iCRP dashboard select Post Inc. → the correct company record. CAC's current FAQ says post-incorporation filings still receive manual officer review.
Match the directors' names and effective dates against the board/shareholder decision and verify whether the same event also changes beneficial ownership before submission.
Submit the application, monitor the dashboard for any CAC query and confirm the updated director information after approval.

After approval, obtain the updated company record or status report and notify banks, regulators and counterparties holding separate director files; a CAC acknowledgement alone may not update those external systems.
notes: Changing a director is different from transferring shares or changing a beneficial owner; use the filing that matches the legal action actually taken.
CAC's published service timelines list director post-registration changes at 12 working hours once a complete filing is received or a query is resolved.
After approval, check the updated company record before relying on the change for banking, contracts or another regulator.
Post-incorporation applications still receive manual approval or queries even though iCRP now uses single sign-on.
Director records and the PSC register are different filings; an ownership-control change can require both.

sources.label: Official agency process and eligibility guidance

title: How to change a company's registered address with CAC
summary: Change the registered office in CAC's company record through the manually reviewed post-incorporation workflow. A relocated shop, operating branch or delivery address is not automatically a legal registered-office amendment.
feeNote: Use the current CAC fee schedule and the amount generated in iCRP for the address-change filing. Late filing can attract additional charges.
timeline: CAC's current service timeline lists 12 working hours for CAC 8/registered-address changes after receipt of the required filing or resolution of a query.
requirements: The company's CAC registration number and authorised iCRP access
The complete new registered-office address, including the building or house number, street, locality, state and other address fields used by CAC
The corporate resolution or approval supporting the registered-office change where the company's governance process requires it
Any address evidence or notice required by the specific CAC post-incorporation transaction
A legible new-office address and supporting corporate approval/evidence required by the chosen address-change transaction.
steps: Confirm that the company is actually changing its legal registered office, rather than only a trading address, branch or shipping location.
Sign in to the CAC iCRP account authorised to manage the company's post-incorporation records.
Open post-incorporation services for the company and select the registered-address change transaction.
Enter the complete new registered-office address and upload the corporate approval or address evidence applicable to the filing.
Review the new address carefully, pay the official filing or late fee generated by iCRP and submit the transaction.
Use iCRP's Post Inc. single sign-on and find the correct company; a change for one RC number must not be applied to a similarly named business.
Validate house number, street, area, LGA, state and effective date against supporting records, and respond to any manual-review query before treating the change as approved.
Monitor any CAC query and, after approval, confirm that the new registered address appears on the updated company record.
After approval, obtain an updated CAC record and separately notify the company's bank, tax authority and relevant licences of the new legal address.
notes: The registered office is the legal address recorded by CAC; moving a shop, branch or operating location does not automatically update that legal record.
CAC's current service timeline lists registered-address changes at 12 working hours once a complete filing is received or a query is resolved.
After the CAC change is approved, update banks, tax authorities and other regulators separately where they maintain their own address records.
CAC post-incorporation submissions remain subject to manual approval rather than the business-name AI review.
An address entered on another regulator's portal does not update the company's CAC statutory address.

title: How to file or update Persons with Significant Control (PSC) with CAC
summary: Report and update the natural persons who ultimately exercise significant control over a CAC company or LLP. PSC details differ from director particulars and require an actual control basis; CAC's Beneficial Ownership Register identifies the five-percent share/vote test alongside other control tests.
feeLabel: CAC filing rules and fees apply
feeNote: PSC information can be reported through incorporation, annual-return or amendment processes as applicable. Use the current iCRP transaction and CAC fee schedule for a paid post-incorporation filing.
timeline: CAC's current service timeline lists 12 working hours for a Change of Person with Significant Control after receipt of the required filing or resolution of a query.
requirements: The company's or LLP's CAC registration details and authorised iCRP access
Full identity and contact particulars of each natural person who meets the current PSC or beneficial-owner test
The shareholding, voting rights, appointment power or other ownership/control basis that makes the person reportable
The date the person became, changed or ceased to be a PSC and the supporting corporate record for that change
Ownership-chain evidence and effective dates showing how the natural person reaches the applicable direct/indirect share, vote or control threshold.
steps: Check CAC's PSC criteria and identify natural persons with direct or indirect shareholding, voting power or other significant control before starting a declaration.
Check CAC's current PSC criteria and identify the natural person or persons who meet the beneficial-owner reporting threshold before filing.
Sign in to CAC iCRP and open the incorporation, annual-return or post-incorporation transaction through which the PSC information must be reported or amended.
Enter each reportable person's identity, ownership or control basis and effective date accurately, then attach the supporting corporate record used for the change.
Review the beneficial-ownership information, complete any official filing charge generated by iCRP and submit the transaction.
Map the control chain and effective dates using ownership records. A change of director alone does not necessarily create or end a reportable PSC.
Use the authorised iCRP incorporation, amendment or annual-return stage for PSC updates and ensure each reported natural person's identity and means of control match the supporting record.
After CAC processes the filing, confirm the updated company record and use the public Beneficial Ownership Register to check the published PSC information.
Check the Beneficial Ownership Register after processing; if the public entry is inconsistent, keep filing evidence and ask CAC how to correct the PSC record.
notes: CAC's Beneficial Ownership Register says the reporting threshold includes a natural person with at least 5% direct or indirect shares or voting rights, or another qualifying form of significant control.
The CAC register states that companies should notify the Commission of acquisition or changes in PSC information within the applicable statutory period.
Beneficial ownership identifies the natural people who ultimately own or control an entity, not merely an intermediary company.
CAC BOR refers to five percent direct or indirect shareholding/votes or other qualifying control, not an automatic report for every director.
PSC information must reflect the human beneficial owners rather than stop at a holding company where further ownership data is required.

title: How to register as a new voter with INEC
summary: A current, source-linked guide to INEC's online registration and pre-registration routes, including the important check for whether a CVR window is active.
feeNote: INEC's current CVR service page does not publish an online application fee for new voter registration. Use only official INEC channels and do not pay an unofficial agent to create a voter record.
requirements: Nigerian citizenship and legal eligibility to register
Age 18 years or older on or before registration day
You must not already have an active voter registration
Access to the official INEC CVR portal and any in-person or biometric step the portal directs you to complete
steps: Open the official INEC CVR portal and read the current service notice first. INEC's published 2025–2026 nationwide CVR timetable ended on 30 August 2026, so confirm that a new registration window is active before relying on an old timetable.
If INEC is accepting new registrations, choose New Voter Online Registration or New Voter Pre-Registration, depending on the route currently offered to you.

Enter the applicant name, contact details and identity information shown on the CVR form. Use the photograph/biometric capture route presented by INEC; for pre-registration, attend the registration centre selected through the official portal to complete biometric enrolment.
Keep the application or registration reference/slip generated by INEC and use the official portal for any follow-up status or PVC collection information.
notes: Do not submit a new registration if you have registered before; INEC warns against double registration.
INEC's voter FAQ states that eligible registrants are Nigerian citizens aged 18 or older who complete the required CVR and biometric enrolment.
This guide is administrative only and does not advise which candidate, party or political choice to support.

title: How to transfer your INEC voter registration
summary: INEC's voter-transfer route changes a registered person's polling location without creating a new voter record. As of 14 October 2026, INEC's main CVR portal says the exercise is not currently active, even though the services directory continues to show Transfers; check its live status before attempting to submit a transfer.
feeNote: INEC's current CVR service page does not publish an online fee for starting a voter-transfer request.
requirements: An existing INEC voter registration
The voter information needed to retrieve your existing registration record
The State and LGA/Area Council for the new voting location, plus the ward or polling-unit option available in the INEC transfer form
Any photograph, identity or supporting step requested by the live portal
steps: Open https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/ and read the official current status message. On 14 October 2026 the main CVR portal says registration is closed; a visible Transfers entry on its separate /Public/getStarted directory does not guarantee a new request will be processed.

When the Commission announces that voter transfers are being accepted again, use the Transfers option on https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/Public/getStarted and sign in to your existing CVR portal account or follow the account-verification instructions.

Retrieve your existing voter registration, check your name and registered polling information, then select the appropriate new destination using INEC's own ward and polling-unit options rather than a third-party map.
Complete only the current identity/photograph and evidence prompts provided by the live INEC transfer process, submit the completed request and securely save the acknowledgement.

Check your record later using INEC's official voter verification/status services. A transfer request slip is not confirmation that the updated voter roll or polling-unit assignment has taken effect; confirm the actual status before travelling.

If you are simply looking for an uncollected PVC or your existing polling unit, use INEC's still-visible existing-voter or polling-unit locator instead of trying to submit a transfer while the CVR exercise is closed.
notes: CURRENT STATUS: INEC's homepage states the CVR exercise has ended as of 14 October 2026. The separate services page still shows Transfers, but it is not evidence of an active nationwide application window.
A transfer changes the voting location on an existing registration. Never register again merely because you have moved home; duplicate voter enrolment is a separate problem.

INEC is the authority for reopening notices, any election-related cutoff, verification of a successful transfer and the exact updated polling unit. Older nationwide 2025–2026 registration schedules should not be reused as dates for future intake windows.
The original INEC portal remains useful for existing-voter PVC status and collection-centre lookup while new CVR activities are marked closed.
This page explains the neutral administrative procedure only; it makes no voting or party recommendation.

title: How to update information on your INEC voter record
summary: INEC's Information Update service lets already registered voters request correction of an existing voter record, not a second enrolment. The main CVR portal currently says the nationwide registration exercise is closed; the separate directory still lists updates, so confirm availability before assuming you can submit corrections online.
feeNote: INEC's current CVR page does not publish an online application fee for its Information Update service.
requirements: An existing INEC voter registration
The existing voter details needed to retrieve your record
Supporting evidence relevant to the correction or update requested
A current photograph/revalidation step if the portal requires it
steps: Visit https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/ and read the main INEC CVR status notice first. As of 14 October 2026 the exercise has ended; availability of the Information Update menu on /Public/getStarted does not mean new submissions are being accepted.
If INEC reopens voter-information updates, choose Information Update at https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/Public/getStarted, then sign in or complete the portal account verification as requested.

Retrieve the original voter record using the identification requested by the live portal. INEC's existing guide describes searching by surname or the last six digits of the Voter Identification Number (VIN); do not create a new registration record.
Verify the record belongs to you, then correct only the affected fields: the documented examples include misspelled names, a legally changed name, gender or date of birth.
Upload any supporting identification or change-of-name evidence requested by INEC for the particular correction, complete the live photograph/identity check and submit the request when available.

Keep INEC's acknowledgement and later confirm through its voter-status/verification system that the correction has actually been reflected. An acknowledgement slip is not confirmation the printed PVC has already changed.

If no online submissions are allowed during closure, use INEC's current status lookup for the existing record and consult INEC iccc@inec.gov.ng or 0700-2255-4632 for the next correction window rather than paying a third party for purported instant editing.
notes: CURRENT STATUS: The main INEC CVR portal says the exercise is closed. The separate service-directory page lists Information Update, but the presence of the menu item is not verification that its form is presently accepting applicants.
Voter-record corrections, polling-unit transfers, lost-PVC replacements and new voter enrolment are four separate administrative services. Do not make a duplicate registration to correct an error.
The documentation required depends on the error. A typo and a legal name change may require different supporting evidence; follow the official form and INEC advice.
If you need to confirm your existing identity record rather than edit it, INEC's separate voter verification service at https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/vvs supports name/birth-date and VIN-based lookups.
A successful submission acknowledgement is different from INEC's eventual processing, voter-roll update or reissued physical card.
This neutral guide is limited to the official administrative record process.

title: INEC Lost or Damaged PVC: Replacement Steps and Current CVR Status
summary: To replace a lost, damaged or defaced Permanent Voter's Card, Nigeria's Electoral Act 2026 section 18 provides for an in-person request to the Electoral Officer or authorised official, no less than 90 days before polling day. INEC's legacy CVR page describes an online request flow, but its live homepage currently says CVR has ended. Check current office procedures with INEC before travelling; do not mistake an older online form for a fully active replacement service.
feeNote: INEC's current CVR page does not publish an online application fee for the Lost or Damaged PVC request.
requirements: An existing registered voter whose original PVC is lost, destroyed, defaced, broken or torn; do not register again just because a card is missing.
Your existing voter identity information or VIN if available, so INEC can match the applicant to the original registered voter record.
A clear explanation of how the card was lost or damaged. Section 18 of the Electoral Act 2026 says you must state the circumstances to the Electoral Officer or authorised official.
For a physically damaged or defaced PVC, keep the original damaged item and any photos requested by INEC; for a missing card, explain the loss rather than inventing a damaged-card photograph.
An in-person visit or appointment with the authorised INEC Electoral Officer/office responsible for your LGA/Area Council, following the latest INEC office directions.
Confirm that you are outside the statutory 90-day before polling-day restricted window; do not rely on outdated online guides implying late issuance is permissible.

Any identity photograph or application slip specifically requested by INEC in its currently authorised process. The old CVR form's two-selfie steps are historical guidance, not a substitute for in-person statutory requirements.
steps: Check https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/ first: as of 14 October 2026 its main page says CVR has ended, although the separate Public/getStarted page still displays a Lost or Damaged PVC menu. A menu entry alone does not establish that a new online request is currently accepted.

Read section 18 of Nigeria's Electoral Act 2026 on the National Assembly's official published Gazette. For a replacement, it directs the owner to apply in person to the electoral officer or an authorised INEC official and describe the loss, destruction, defacement or damage, at least 90 days before polling day.

Contact INEC's Citizens Contact Centre at iccc@inec.gov.ng or its published official hotlines to confirm which LGA/Area Council office or authorised officer is receiving replacement requests now, the timetable, and what evidence or appointment to bring. Do not pay anyone who promises an instant card.

Check your existing registration before making the trip. Use the main CVR portal's Find My PVC function or INEC's verification tool at https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/vvs to locate your registration using the supported name/date-of-birth or VIN search.

Prepare your registration information and a truthful statement of what happened to the original PVC. If the card is physically damaged, retain it as supporting evidence. Do not submit a separate new voter registration or make a duplicate identity.

If INEC instructs you to attend its Electoral Officer, apply personally following that official process and ask for the appropriate acknowledgment. Section 18 says a physical replacement, when issued, should be clearly marked REPLACEMENT.

Treat INEC's older online replacement flow as background only: it describes signing in, retrieving the existing record, selecting lost/damaged reason, uploading a damaged-card image if relevant, and taking two self photographs. Those steps must not be presented as sufficient when the current law requires an in-person application.

Keep any authorised receipt/slip but separately verify that the replacement PVC has been produced and the correct collection centre is open. An application receipt is not a card-collection appointment.

INEC's CVR services page also lists a downloadable PVC pilot for eligible Osun State voters, described as coming soon for wider use. The 2026 Act preserves the possibility of printing a downloadable copy, but it does not prove that the digital service is available to all voters today.
notes: CURRENT LAW: Electoral Act 2026 section 18 directs the owner of a lost or damaged card to apply in person to the Electoral Officer or another duly authorised officer at least 90 days before polling day. The same section prohibits issuance of a replacement less than 90 days before polling day and mentions the possibility of printing a downloadable copy.

CURRENT PORTAL STATUS: INEC's CVR homepage says the registration exercise is not currently active as of 14 October 2026, despite the continued Lost/Damaged PVC link on the separate service page. An online services directory is not proof of an open application window.

OLDER ONLINE INSTRUCTIONS: An earlier INEC article on a legacy website described self-service account registration, two identity photos and upload of an image for a physically damaged card. That is useful history, but the current 2026 law and INEC's present official instructions take precedence; do not claim those historical steps complete the legal replacement procedure.

Different scenarios need different evidence: preserve and bring a torn/defaced card if available, or explain an actual loss honestly. Never invent a damaged-card image or claim a card was lost when it is available.

INEC's official voter verification service can still identify an existing registration from VIN or registered name and birth date. A record not found should be escalated through INEC, not repaired by creating a duplicate voter enrolment.

INEC's 2026 Gazette provides that the original PVC is replaced by another copy marked REPLACEMENT when the authorised officer is satisfied; the legal distinction matters if an agent offers an unmarked photocopy as an official card.

The main CVR service listing calls downloadable PVC an eligible Osun State pilot / coming-soon feature. Although the 2026 Act mentions printing a downloadable copy, availability and authorised use must be verified through current INEC channels; do not advertise nationwide live printing.

Neither the current CVR homepage nor the checked national statute establishes a universal 'same-day card', current replacement charge or guaranteed pickup date. Confirm fees, documents, date and responsible office directly with INEC.
Voter-card replacement, transfer of polling location and correcting an existing name or date of birth are separate processes. A replacement is not automatic permission to change where you vote.

INEC's contact centre publishes iccc@inec.gov.ng and phone channels at https://www.inecnigeria.org/contact/. Confirm the currently listed numbers and operating hours there instead of relying on private WhatsApp 'PVC agents'.

The main CVR homepage currently marks the registration window closed; contact INEC before travelling or assuming an online replacement is open.

title: How to find your INEC PVC pickup location
summary: INEC's Uncollected PVC service helps previously registered voters identify where to collect an uncollected Permanent Voter Card. The collection point may change during temporary distribution exercises, so confirm the current INEC announcement before travelling. INEC rules require collection in person; an agent, friend or relative cannot collect the PVC by proxy.
feeNote: INEC's current portal does not state a fee for using the Uncollected PVC pickup-location lookup.
requirements: A prior INEC voter registration; the service does not enrol a first-time voter.
The registered voter's name and previous registration identity information used by INEC's Uncollected PVC search; match the record before relying on the result.
The registered voter's own presence and any registration slip or identity evidence used at the designated collection point.
A current official INEC collection notice if the local centre or schedule has changed.
steps: Open the official INEC CVR portal and select the Uncollected PVC service for someone already registered to vote.
Use the voter details the lookup accepts and record the pickup location that matches the registered person's record.
Cross-check the location and collection dates against current INEC State Office/LGA announcements; an old election's temporary collection centre might no longer operate.
Prepare the voter registration slip if available and the identity evidence needed for INEC's collection officer to find the voter in the register.
Attend the designated INEC pickup point personally; the Commission's guidelines expressly forbid PVC collection by proxy.
Ask the officer to confirm the registered voter's record before card handover and complete the collection acknowledgment requested by INEC.
If the record says collected or the centre cannot locate the card, request an official INEC check rather than paying a third party or using the polling-unit locator as a substitute.
notes: PVC collection point and election-day polling unit are different locations; the latter lookup cannot tell you where uncollected cards are stored.
INEC permits verification of identity where the voter has lost the registration slip, but still requires personal attendance.
The portal lookup is an administrative service and does not guarantee that cards are available for same-day pickup.
No fee is stated for the ordinary uncollected PVC location lookup.

title: How to find your INEC polling unit
summary: INEC's official polling-unit locator directs registered voters to their assigned voting location by State, LGA and Registration Area/Ward and returns the polling-unit location description and coordinates when available. The polling unit is where the voter is accredited and votes, not the INEC office used to collect an uncollected PVC.
feeNote: INEC's official polling-unit directory and locator do not state a fee for looking up a polling unit.
requirements: The State and LGA of the existing voter registration, not merely the current city or residence.
The ward/Registration Area (RA) and polling-unit number or code where known.
An internet connection to INEC's official cvr.inecnigeria.org/pu polling-unit tool.
The voter's existing PVC or voter record to cross-check any returned unit.
steps: Open https://inecnigeria.org/polling-units/ and use the official Find Polling Unit link to the INEC CVR locator.
Check the polling-unit code printed on the PVC if available, then choose State of registration, LGA and Ward/Registration Area.
Select or search the listed polling unit, checking the official unit name and location description rather than guessing from a nearby school or landmark.
Use available coordinates/directions carefully and compare the displayed unit with the PVC or voter record before election-day travel.
If the locator shows a unit different from an old screenshot, consult the current INEC voter-record or transfer service; updating a registered unit is not achieved just by visiting a closer one.
For PVC collection, use the separate Uncollected PVC lookup instead of travelling to the polling unit to request the card.
notes: INEC lists 176,846 polling units across the 36 states and FCT; this guide concerns locating one assigned unit.
The public locator is free and does not itself change an existing voter registration.
A voter ordinarily votes at their registered unit, subject to INEC's applicable voter-record rules and an approved transfer.
Keep official civic instructions neutral; MyNigeriaGuide does not endorse any party or candidate.

For an existing application, keep the relevant application, passport or payment reference available
For an in-person consular service, check the embassy's current appointment and document instructions before travelling
steps: Open the official Embassy of Nigeria in the Netherlands website and choose the relevant consular service or contact page.
For general enquiries, use the embassy's published contact details at Wagenaarweg 5, 2597 LL The Hague, Netherlands, or the official phone/email channels on its contact page.
If your request concerns a passport or visa, follow the service-specific instructions and online application route before arranging any required embassy appointment.
For a lost passport or urgent travel-document problem, use the embassy's official emergency or Emergency Travel Certificate guidance and keep the required police or identity evidence.
Before travelling to the embassy, confirm the current appointment requirement, opening arrangement and documents on the official site.

The embassy FAQ lists consular services from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

title: How to check the JAMB matriculation list
summary: JAMB's matriculation-list check indicates whether the Board recognises the student's admission for the relevant institutional record, which matters for NYSC mobilisation. Start with the public JAMB checker. If the name is absent, JAMB directs students to obtain their official admission letter and result slip and take them to the institution's admissions officer for verification; repeatedly checking the page does not correct a missing admission.
feeLabel: Free to check the matriculation list
feeNote: JAMB's matriculation-list checker itself does not show a fee. If you need to print a JAMB result slip or admission letter to complete the process, JAMB lists each document service separately on its payment-services page.
timeline: The online check is immediate once you enter the required examination details and registration number. Fixing a missing record depends on completing the required JAMB documents and your institution verifying them.
requirements: JAMB registration number
Examination year/type used for the admission
Access to your JAMB e-Facility records if you need to print your result slip or admission letter
steps: Open https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng/CheckMatriculationList and select the examination type/year requested on the public form.
Enter the JAMB registration number accurately, then submit the matriculation-list lookup.
If the candidate is listed, compare the name and available record details with the institution's admission and keep the result for reference.
If the name is missing, sign in to the genuine JAMB e-Facility profile and check the admission status before buying a document.
Print the official JAMB result slip and admission letter using their separate e-Facility services if JAMB says either is outstanding.
Present both documents to the institution's admissions officer to complete the verification JAMB describes, and ask the institution to confirm that its admissions record is corrected.
Recheck the JAMB matriculation list later; do not substitute a school-generated admission notice for a missing JAMB admission record.
notes: The public matriculation-list lookup is free, while generating an official result slip and admission letter can be charged separately.
A missing name is an issue to reconcile with the institution/JAMB, not a cue to buy third-party 'NYSC clearance'.
Institutional corrections may not display immediately after uploading documents; do not promise a guaranteed date.

title: How JAMB regularization / condonement of illegal admission works
summary: Understand JAMB's current condonement route for an admission that was not originally processed through JAMB and the official service fee before starting.
feeNote: JAMB's Payment & Services page lists Condonement of Illegal Admission (Foreign/Local) at ₦10,000, with a ₦300 CBT service charge.
timeline: There is no single public completion time. The process can depend on institution-side confirmation and JAMB review after the required service is initiated.
requirements: A JAMB profile/e-Facility account tied to the admission record you need to regularise
The institution, programme, admission year and other admission particulars shown on your school record
A payment method accepted by the JAMB e-Facility service after the transaction is generated
steps: Sign in to the official JAMB e-Facility portal with the profile connected to the admission record you need to regularise.
Open the admission-related service area and choose the current Condonement of Illegal Admission service that matches a local or foreign admission record.
Generate the JAMB service transaction, review the displayed ₦10,000 service fee and ₦300 CBT service charge, then complete payment through the approved payment option shown in e-Facility.
Complete the admission particulars requested in the condonement application and save the acknowledgement or transaction reference generated by JAMB.

Present or submit the acknowledgement and admission evidence to your institution when JAMB requires institution-side confirmation, then return to e-Facility to confirm that the admission record has been updated.
notes: JAMB currently labels this paid service 'Condonement of Illegal Admission (Foreign/Local)' on its Payment & Services page.
Do not pay an agent outside the official JAMB/approved CBT route.

title: How to search and verify a company or business on CAC Public Search
summary: Check a Nigerian entity using CAC's public registry by legal name, RC/BN registration number or AV Code; compare the exact record rather than trusting an invoice's company name. Public Search is not proof that the salesperson is authorised, nor a paid E-Status Report/Certified True Copy.
feeLabel: Basic public search is available online
feeNote: CAC's public-search page provides the search interface. Paid documents such as a Certified True Copy or status report are separate CAC services.
timeline: Basic search results are returned online after you submit the search details.
requirements: An official entity name, RC/BN registration number or AV code to enter in CAC's public search field.
Another independent entity identifier, such as address or entity type, to distinguish similar company names.
A current source for comparison when acting on a contract, invoice or bank-payment request.
An independent registration number or other identifier to distinguish a genuine registry entry from a lookalike.
steps: Get an independent legal name and RC/BN number from a genuine entity document, then open CAC Public Search yourself instead of following a payment-request message.
Open the genuine CAC Public Search at https://icrp.cac.gov.ng/public-search/ without buying a third-party search subscription.
Choose the search method shown and enter the legal name, RC number or AV code exactly as supplied by the company.
Read the returned list and choose the matching entity rather than assuming the first similarly named business is the intended company.
Compare the registration number, legal entity type and status against the documents or invoice you are verifying.
If CAC provides limited public details, request the separate CAC Status Report or Certified True Copy rather than altering a public-search screenshot.
Use a second identifier such as registration number, entity type or state to distinguish similarly named records and avoid false matches.
For a large transaction, ask the entity for an authorised representative's identity and, when required, an official CAC Status Report/CTC; a public search cannot verify control of a bank account.
Keep a record of the official lookup for your internal checks, but use a formally issued CAC document when a bank, legal office or procurement team requires certified proof.
If no matching record is found or the details conflict, postpone the transaction and request a CAC-issued explanation or formal record; do not alter screenshots to make an entity appear registered.
notes: The CAC portal's placeholder explicitly accepts 'Entity name, RC number, or AV code'.
Public Search is accessible without the pre-incorporation user registration flow; registering a company or requesting certified documents is different.
A match confirms a registry entry but does not establish that every salesperson using the company name is authorised.
Do not confuse CAC basic search with CAC name reservation when forming a new company.
A valid CAC entry is not a warranty that an unrelated seller, bank account or social-media page genuinely represents that company.
CAC E-Status Reports and CTCs are separate documentary evidence and are not generated by the free public search alone.

sources.label: Official agency process and eligibility guidance

title: How to validate a BVN with NIBSS *565*1#
summary: NIBSS *565*1# validates whether an 11-digit BVN exists and displays the name recorded against it, for a published ₦20 USSD fee. This is distinct from the owner's BVN retrieval (*565*0#) and does not prove control of the linked bank account or authorise sharing personal identifiers.
feeNote: NIBSS states that BVN validation through *565*1# carries a ₦20 service fee.
timeline: The validation result is returned during the USSD session.
requirements: The 11-digit BVN you want to validate
A Nigerian mobile line that can dial NIBSS *565# USSD services
At least ₦20 airtime for the NIBSS BVN-validation service charge
Permission to perform an identity validation, and a number transmitted through a secure channel rather than an unsolicited public post.
steps: Only validate an eleven-digit BVN for an authorised identity-checking purpose; ask the individual whose record is involved to supply it securely rather than harvesting BVNs from documents.
Open the phone dialler on a Nigerian mobile line and dial *565*1# to start the NIBSS BVN-validation service.
Read the validation response and compare the returned registered name with the person or record you are checking before relying on the BVN.
Dial *565*1#, enter the eleven digits and review them before sending to avoid paying for a mistyped lookup.
Read the name supplied by NIBSS and compare it with the independently presented identification; spelling or identity mismatches should be resolved with the bank.
Do not assume that a valid number and matching name proves that a caller owns a bank account or is authorised to receive payment; confirm the account independently with the bank.
If the USSD lookup cannot run, check airtime and service availability before retrying. NIBSS publishes a ₦20 charge, and repeated calls are unnecessary once the result is recorded.
notes: NIBSS says the service confirms that a BVN is correct and returns the name registered to the BVN.
This is different from retrieving your own forgotten BVN with *565*0#.
The service discloses a name, so treat the returned output as sensitive personal data and avoid exposing it in messages or screenshots.
BVN validation is not a way to change an enrollee's name or date of birth; the bank's amendment procedure handles corrections.

title: How to correct or update BVN details
summary: Correct a BVN-linked name, date of birth or permitted demographic field through an authorised bank, not a third-party online BVN 'editor'. The CBN framework limits birth-date corrections to one supported change, and its May 2026 rule allows the BVN-linked mobile number to be changed only once; collect bank evidence before submitting.
feeLabel: No single central BVN-update fee is published by CBN
feeNote: CBN sets the conditions for allowed BVN record changes. Your bank handles the customer update process and may provide its own current operational requirements.
timeline: CBN guidance states that BVN issue resolution should be completed within five working days once all required documents have been submitted.
requirements: Your existing BVN and a valid government-issued identity document
A completed BVN data-amendment form supplied by the bank handling the correction
For a name change: the legal evidence accepted for the change, such as a marriage certificate, divorce document, court order or other bank-accepted supporting record
For a date-of-birth correction: documentary evidence showing the correct date of birth, noting that the CBN framework permits this correction only once
The original and proposed field values, legal supporting evidence and any historic BVN amendments already completed.
steps: Identify which field is wrong on your existing BVN record and compare it against the supporting government ID or civil document before requesting a BVN amendment at your bank.
Visit or contact the bank that will handle the BVN amendment and request its current BVN data-amendment form for the exact field you need to correct.
Complete the amendment form with your existing BVN and the corrected demographic information exactly as supported by your identity records.
Submit the completed form, valid identification and the supporting document for the requested name, date-of-birth or other permitted correction.
Complete the identity or biometric verification requested by the bank and collect a reference, acknowledgement or complaint ticket for the submitted amendment.
Check the updated BVN record through your bank after processing and escalate the request to the bank if a complete submission remains unresolved beyond the applicable handling period.
For a birth-date correction, ask the bank to review the civil evidence and the once-only amendment restriction before submission. The bank may reject unsupported conflicting dates.
For a name change due to marriage, divorce or court process, assemble the exact certificate or court document the bank accepts instead of asking for an arbitrary spelling replacement.
For a phone-number change, confirm which line should be permanently linked because CBN's May 2026 rules allow only one change.
Keep the bank's dated amendment ticket and later check the linked account or bank BVN record. A bank account profile update may not mean the BVN registry has synchronised.
If another bank still sees the old record, report the mismatch to the original amending bank with the ticket rather than opening a second BVN.
notes: CBN allows date-of-birth correction once with supporting documents and permits supported name changes and minor corrections.
A BVN itself does not change when the underlying customer record is corrected.
The CBN framework limits supported date-of-birth corrections to one change. Check your supporting records carefully with the bank before submitting this particular amendment.
CBN's reforms effective May 2026 restrict BVN-linked phone-number changes to one.
Only authorised institutions can access the BVN database; do not upload original identifiers to purported public BVN 'update' sites.

title: Tax ID Nigeria: How to Retrieve Your TIN with NIN or CAC
summary: Retrieve Nigeria's harmonised Tax ID (TIN) on the official NRS/JRB portal using NIN for individuals or CAC registration details for businesses.
feeLabel: No fee is shown on the official Tax ID retrieval portal
feeNote: The official Tax ID portal presents retrieval as an online identity-confirmation service and does not display a retrieval fee on the public workflow.
timeline: The portal checks the submitted identity details online; successful matching can display the recognised Tax ID during the retrieval process.
requirements: Individuals: your 11-digit NIN and the personal identity information used on the NIMC record
Registered companies or business entities: the CAC registration number or registered entity information accepted by the Tax ID portal
Access to a phone or computer that can complete the Tax ID portal's identity check
steps: Open the official Nigerian Tax ID portal and choose the Tax ID retrieval option.
Select Individual, Corporate or the entity type that matches the taxpayer whose Tax ID you need.
For an individual, enter the NIN and matching personal identity fields; for a registered organisation, enter the CAC registration information requested by the portal.
Complete the portal security check and submit the identity match request.
Review and save the Tax ID returned by the official portal, or correct the underlying NIN/CAC identity record first if the portal reports a mismatch.
notes: NRS/JRB describe the Tax ID as a harmonised national tax identity linked to foundational records such as NIN for individuals and CAC registration for businesses.
The official portal says a valid Tax ID is required for many public and private services, including banking, employment documentation, government contracts and statutory filings.
If identity records do not match, the portal can require the underlying NIN/CAC record to be corrected first.

title: How to track a Nigerian passport application
summary: Track your Nigerian passport at track.immigration.gov.ng with the Application Number and Reference Number from the same NIS submission. If you need to find a payment receipt instead, use the domestic passport portal's separate status/receipt lookup; payment confirmation does not mean your passport is ready.
feeLabel: No fee is shown for the online status check
feeNote: The NIS tracking page provides the application-status lookup. Any passport application or issuance fee is separate from checking status.
timeline: A successful lookup displays the status currently published by NIS; the tracker does not establish a fixed processing or passport-collection deadline.
requirements: Your exact Application Number from the official NIS passport submission confirmation
Your corresponding Reference Number from the same application or acknowledgement
Access to the original confirmation email or saved receipt to re-check the numbers if a lookup fails
steps: Open the official Nigeria Immigration Service tracking website at https://track.immigration.gov.ng/ and use its passport application status form.
Find the Application Number on the NIS acknowledgement or confirmation message and enter it exactly as issued.
Enter the Reference Number for that same application; do not substitute a payment receipt number or another person's application details.
Choose View Application Status and read the status displayed by NIS. A valid number pair is needed; MyNigeriaGuide does not store your passport numbers.

If you still have the Reference Number, the domestic NIS passport portal's separate Payment Status/Print Receipt search accepts it plus your Application Number, date of birth or email to look up receipt details. That is not a substitute for the two-number tracking checker.

Follow any separate official NIS appointment, biometrics or collection instruction shown in your account or communication. Do not treat payment completion alone as proof that a passport has been printed.
notes: The passport status tracker asks for both an Application Number and a Reference Number; these are different fields and both are required.

The domestic NIS portal's Payment Status/Print Receipt search accepts a Reference Number with an Application Number, date of birth or email. It checks application/payment records; the dedicated passport tracker still requires both Application and Reference Numbers. Payment confirmation, appointment booking, production and collection are different stages.
If the online checker cannot find an application, first verify that both numbers belong to the same submission. Use NIS's published help/contact channels for unresolved cases.
Only follow an NIS confirmation to visit a passport office; do not rely on a WhatsApp agent promising immediate printing, collection or a guaranteed delivery day.

title: How to verify a Nigerian driver's licence
summary: FRSC offers two different driver's-licence verification routes: a public RID/licence-number document check and an institutional verification request. The quick check at ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/verify is not a paid certificate-delivery order. For official organisational requests, FRSC requires an agency recipient address and can charge for verification and shipping; personal or residential recipient addresses are not accepted.
feeLabel: Public RID check; formal institutional verification/shipping may cost extra
feeNote: The quick RID/licence-number check is a public lookup. FRSC's separate agency-directed verification requests can attract verification or shipping charges; check that workflow before paying.
timeline: The public verification check is performed online after you submit the RID or licence number.
requirements: The document's RID number or driver's-licence number for the public lookup.
The original record or licence to compare with the portal's returned identity and issuance details.
If requesting formal verification for an organisation, authorised organisation details and an agency receiving address.
For a formal delivery request, portal account access and the verification/shipping payment requested by FRSC.
steps: For a direct public check, open https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/verify, not a third-party validation page.
Type the RID number or Nigerian driver's-licence number in the single lookup field and submit Verify Document.

Compare the response with the supplied licence, especially the registered number, holder and issuance details. Treat missing or conflicting data as requiring FRSC follow-up rather than proof of fraud on its own.
For an official document sent to an institution, return to the main FRSC verification portal and register/sign in as the authorised requester.
Complete its verification form, enter the government/private/non-governmental organisation's delivery address, confirm any verification and shipping charges and submit the paid request.
Track delivery using the tracking number FRSC issues and record confirmation of receipt after the agency gets the document.
If the public lookup fails or the formal record conflicts, send the RID and issue date to the verification support contact on the official portal.
notes: FRSC says formal verification applications addressed to individuals or residential addresses are not processed, even if payment was made.
The public RID lookup and formal paid verification/shipping flow are not the same product.
The verification portal lists verification@ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng for document-check complaints and verification@frsc.gov.ng for main service requests.
A lookup cannot substitute for licence renewal, category upgrade or replacement.

title: NINAuth App: Generate a NIN Sharecode, Scan QR and Download Your NIN Slip
summary: Use NIMC's official NINAuth app to consent to identity verification with a participating organisation using a short-lived Sharecode or organisation QR code. NIMC also added free official NIN-slip downloads via Do More with NINAuth in June 2026. This service uses an existing NIN; it does not enrol you for a new number.
feeLabel: NINAuth app / NIN slip download: free
feeNote: NIMC's June 2026 NINAuth announcement expressly says downloading an official NIN slip within the app is free. The general individuals page does not advertise a charge for app download or Sharecode generation; businesses and verification service providers may have different charges. Avoid agents charging to provide the already-free slip.
timeline: A Sharecode is designed to be time-limited, and an eligible verification can take place during the app session once your profile is active and the partner supports NINAuth. The published public instructions do not guarantee a fixed number of minutes for every code or resolve a failed verification without the participating organisation.
requirements: An existing National Identification Number: NINAuth is a verification and digital-identity service, not a substitute for first-time NIMC enrolment.
A compatible Android or iOS smartphone and access to the official NINAuth app from NIMC's download page; meet any NIMC age/guardian-consent requirements.
An activated NINAuth profile linked to your existing NIN and any onboarding identity checks the app requests.
For a Sharecode verification, an organisation that explicitly accepts NINAuth Sharecodes; for QR verification, an organisation-provided QR code.
For free NIN slip download, a current version of NINAuth showing the Do More with NINAuth feature and its NIN Slip option.
Read the organisation's request before granting permission to share any name, date of birth, photograph or other identity attributes.
steps: Open https://ninauth.nimc.gov.ng/download rather than a third-party APK or a website advertising paid NINAuth Sharecodes. Use NIMC's official Android or iOS store link, install the app and follow its current onboarding instructions with your existing NIN.

Activate and secure the account using the identity and device checks the app requires. Do not supply your app password, verification code or biometrics to an agent. If you do not yet have a NIN, use the separate NIMC enrolment service before attempting NINAuth verification.

If a bank, telecom operator, recruitment portal or government service asks for a NINAuth Sharecode, open the Sharecode function in your NINAuth profile and generate a fresh time-limited code. Give it only to the named organisation as part of a verification you initiated.

If the organisation presents a NINAuth QR code instead, use the app's Scan QR / Scan Code feature to read that organisation's code. A random QR code from a social-media poster is not proof it belongs to an authorised identity-verification partner.

Review which identity details the requesting service wants. Approve only the verification or data-sharing request you recognise. A NINAuth Sharecode is for consent-based verification; it is not a replacement for all KYC requirements or permission to share your raw NIN publicly.

Confirm that the requesting organisation received the verification result; if it fails or the code expires, begin a fresh request rather than repeatedly forwarding an old Sharecode. Ask the organisation whether its own integration and accepted verification method are operational.

To download your official NIN slip for free, update NINAuth to the latest version, open Do More with NINAuth, tap NIN Slip, then download and securely save the document. NIMC's 18 June 2026 update says this is the same valid slip previously obtained through NIMC channels.

Keep a slip private and share only when required. A downloaded document is useful for presenting a printable identity record; it does not grant another organisation permission to silently access all data in your app.

If the Sharecode, QR scanner or NIN Slip option is missing, confirm the app is updated and that you are signed in to the official NIMC product. The public site lists the supported features, but real deployment, minimum age and identity-match issues may vary; use official NINAuth support instead of an unofficial agent.
notes: NIMC's official Get Started guide supports two organisation-facing workflows: scanning the organisation's NINAuth QR code or producing a unique time-limited Sharecode for a compatible verifier. Which option appears depends on the service you are using, and not every business has integrated NINAuth.

NINAuth uses existing NIN data for consent-based identification and verification; it does not register a first-time NIN. A failed identity match needs correction through recognised NIMC routes, not the purchase of another NIN.

NIMC officially launched NINAuth in May 2025 and published its Do More with NINAuth/NIN Slip download feature on 18 June 2026. Guides that only describe identity verification miss this later free document service.

To download the free official slip, the published NIMC instructions say: Do More with NINAuth → NIN Slip → Download. This is a NIMC-published feature, not a third-party PDF generation website. Keep the latest app version.

NINAuth says the slip can be presented in settings such as banks and government offices that require a physical or printable NIN slip. Acceptance of any other identity document, QR code or partner workflow still depends on the requesting organisation.

NIMC's download page says users must have a NIN, meet minimum-age conditions and agree to its terms; users under 18 may require parent or guardian consent. Do not claim every minor can use every app feature without restriction.

Protect your NIN and any verification Sharecode. Sharecodes are temporary by design, but should still be given only for an intended application. If you receive an unexpected request or an unfamiliar QR code, do not approve it.

The public NINAuth individual pages do not set a universal individual Sharecode fee, expiry minute count or promised success rate. Avoid paying agents based on invented OTP-like charges or assuming every NINAuth integration accepts one code format.
The free NIN slip download within NINAuth should not be confused with having to order a plastic national identity card. It is the official printable slip rather than a new NIN assignment.

Some older guides use the labels 'NIN validation', 'NIN verification', 'Sharecode' and 'NIN Slip' interchangeably. Validation/identity sharing is an in-app consent interaction; the slip is a document to save or print; first-time NIN enrolment is a separate service.

title: How to check or retrieve your NIN with *346#
summary: To retrieve an existing 11-digit NIN, dial *346# on the telephone line you registered with NIMC and follow the retrieval prompt (the NCC describes option 1). NIMC's February 2026 Service Charter lists ₦50 for *346# retrieval. You can instead check an existing official NIMC ID record or contact NIMC if the registered SIM has been lost.
feeNote: NIMC's February 2026 Service Charter, section 16.6, lists ₦50 for 'NIN Retrieval (via 346#)'. This supersedes the older ₦20 charge/temporary fee waiver described in some historical NCC FAQs. Check your actual network USSD prompt before accepting a deduction.
requirements: An NIN must already have been issued; *346# does not enrol a first-time applicant.
An active Nigerian mobile line that matches the phone number provided during NIMC registration, as NCC specifies.
At least the published ₦50 retrieval fee available as airtime if the network charges as listed in NIMC's current service charter.
If the registered SIM is lost or no retrieval result appears, enough identity evidence to seek assistance through a genuine NIMC office or operator.
steps: Confirm whether your NIN is already printed on the NIMC slip issued during enrolment; it is normally the 11-digit number on that document. Do not pay for a fresh retrieval if you already have it.
From the mobile number previously registered with NIMC, dial *346#. Choose the NIN retrieval option shown on the menu; NCC's published guidance describes pressing 1.
Read the fee prompt before proceeding. NIMC's February 2026 Service Charter states ₦50 for *346# retrieval; old pages mentioning a temporary ₦20 waiver should not be used as the current fee.
Complete the USSD prompts and keep the returned 11-digit NIN private. Never share a screenshot of your full NIN or OTP publicly or with an unofficial agent.

If the lookup says the phone number is not linked to a NIN, check that you are using the originally registered SIM. NCC advises calling your telecom provider if USSD returns an error; NIMC can assist at an official centre with forgotten records.
If you are attempting to link a SIM rather than retrieve the number, use your network operator's own NIN-linking channel; *346# is the retrieval step, not the complete mobile-line linkage process.
notes: The NCC explicitly distinguishes retrieval via *346# from NIN–SIM linking. The line used for retrieval must match the NIMC enrolment record.
NIMC's February 2026 published schedule lists ₦50 for the *346# lookup; an older NCC FAQ mentioned a time-limited ₦20 fee waiver during the original SIM-link campaign.
The 11-digit NIN is not the same as a virtual NIN, share code or the separate *346*2*Your NIN# Mobile ID function, which needs the NIN you already know.
NIMC provides an in-person fallback when the registered phone cannot retrieve an existing NIN. Do not use fake 'instant retrieval' sites or give strangers your identity number.

title: How to book a Nigerian passport appointment
summary: A Nigerian passport appointment is booked against an actual NIS application after selecting the relevant fresh, renewal/reissue or correction service. The portal has separate Check Centre Availability and Book Appointment tools; the first merely previews possible dates. Applicants must retain their payment and appointment slips and attend in person for NIS photograph/biometric capture.
feeNote: NIS lists Book Appointment under the application services, but does not advertise an independent flat booking fee. Review the underlying passport fee before payment.
timeline: Appointment availability depends on the selected processing centre; use the live NIS portal for the date currently offered.
requirements: A genuine existing NIS passport application and access to the account or application reference.
The applicant's correct passport/NIN and contact details supplied on the original form.
A processing centre that can handle the specific passport route and available booking date.
The application/payment and appointment slips plus original supporting documents for the eventual visit.
steps: Go to https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and choose the appropriate domestic route; people applying abroad should use the international portal and mission instructions.
Before submitting, use Check Centre Availability to compare the earliest dates at realistic processing centres; this does not reserve a slot.
Complete the required fresh, renewal/reissue or correction application and review the NIS fee shown for that actual transaction.
Select Book Appointment or resume the existing application and sign in with the details attached to the original passport record.
Choose an available processing centre and date, check the confirmation and save/print the appointment slip along with the official payment receipt.
Bring the supporting civil/identity documents and, for renewal or correction, the existing passport booklet to the scheduled NIS office.
Appear personally for photograph and biometric capture, then use Application Status/Print Receipt to follow the record; do not assume the appointment itself means issuance is approved.
notes: Availability and appointment confirmation are different screens and different stages.
Any passport application fee is separate from checking centre availability; do not purchase 'queue access' from private agents.
For applications from abroad, the responsible Nigerian Embassy/High Commission/Consulate gives local attendance instructions.

title: How to check Nigerian passport centre availability

requirements: Access to the official NIS domestic passport application portal from a browser.
A shortlist of processing centres the applicant can attend for biometric enrolment.
The intended fresh-passport, renewal or change-of-data route and supporting documents for that service.
steps: Visit https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and confirm you are applying from within Nigeria. If abroad, choose Apply from outside Nigeria instead.
Under Before you Proceed choose Check Centre Availability; this is separate from Book Appointment.
Compare the displayed earliest appointment dates at the processing centres that are practical for you to reach.
Consider the processing office's location and document requirements before selecting it for the actual passport application.
Open the appropriate Fresh Passport, Renewal/Re-issue or Correction of Data service, complete the application and make only official payments.
Use Book Appointment when the application allows it; select an offered slot, confirm and save the appointment and payment slips.
Recheck your booked date from the official application account before travelling, because an availability preview alone does not hold a place.
notes: The earliest date reported by the lookup may disappear before a booking is completed.
Do not pay an unofficial agent to claim or hold an advertised slot.
NIS requires personal attendance for photograph and biometric enrolment at the applicable passport office.
Diaspora users have a separate passport route and relevant Nigerian mission instructions.

title: How to test a Nigerian passport photo online
summary: NIS provides a Test Photo Upload pre-application checker on its domestic passport portal. It lets an applicant verify whether a proposed passport-sized digital photograph meets the portal's upload rules before beginning a paid passport transaction. Passing the photograph precheck does not cancel the later requirement for NIS biometric capture.
timeline: The tool is intended as a pre-application compliance check; no separate service timeline is published on the portal.
requirements: A recent, clear digital portrait of the same person named in the passport application.
A browser/device able to choose and upload the digital photograph.
A photograph that meets the live portal's file-format, size and image-composition requirements; follow its displayed rules rather than unverified dimensions.
steps: Open the official domestic NIS passport portal at https://passport.immigration.gov.ng/ and open its photo checker.
Find Test Photo Upload under Before you Proceed, rather than beginning a fresh paid application solely to check an image.

Read the precise result or rejection reason shown, such as quality, dimensions or upload failure, without assuming every upload error means the photograph is unacceptable.
If it fails, replace or recrop the photo to satisfy the live checker and try again with the revised image.
After a successful precheck, begin the correct Fresh, Renewal/Re-issue or Change of Data application and keep the image available if the form requests it.

After the photo precheck, select Book Appointment from the actual NIS passport application, save the appointment slip and attend the selected NIS processing office for photograph and biometric capture.
notes: NIS does not publish a universal separate charge for this pre-application checker.
An acceptable digital upload does not guarantee that NIS will accept all of the application documents.
Never upload passport portraits, NIN or birth certificates to a third-party site claiming NIS photo certification.
feeNote: NIS lists Test Photo Upload as a pre-application tool; the paid passport transaction remains a separate service.

title: How Nigeria's Emergency Travel Certificate works
summary: A stranded Nigerian abroad with a missing, stolen or expired passport should ask the nearest Nigerian mission which emergency return document it currently issues. NIS describes an Emergency Travel Certificate and has announced a replacement biometric Single Travel Emergency Passport (STEP). This route may be limited to a particular homebound journey and must not be presented as a general-purpose substitute for a regular passport.
feeLabel: Mission-dependent emergency document charge; confirm first
timeline: NIS advertises under 72 hours for ETC, but timing and STEP availability must be verified with the relevant mission.
requirements: Evidence of Nigerian identity/citizenship accepted by the responsible embassy or consulate.
Any available passport biodata copy or details of the lost, expired or stolen passport.
Police loss/theft report or other declaration if the local mission demands it.
Confirmed travel itinerary/destination and other documentary requirements announced by the issuing mission.
steps: Contact the nearest official Nigerian Embassy, High Commission or Consulate and explain the passport problem and intended journey.
Ask whether that mission currently issues the old Emergency Travel Certificate, the announced STEP document, or another approved emergency travel document.
Confirm that the document type is accepted for your particular departure, transit and intended arrival before paying for onward tickets.
Prepare the mission's identity/citizenship, former passport and loss/theft or expiry evidence, including police documentation if requested.
Book the actual mission appointment or use the official emergency channel it specifies and pay only fees shown by that authority.
Complete the required identity/capture process, obtain written issuance/collection information and carefully review the permitted direction and validity.
Carry the original emergency travel document plus any airline/transit documentation; for a normal future international trip, arrange a regular passport instead.
notes: The current NIS homepage advertises an Emergency Travel Certificate, while a separate NIS announcement describes STEP as a replacement: verify actual availability with the local mission.
A general NIS statement about processing in less than 72 hours is not a commitment by every mission or for every case.
Avoid purchasing a supposedly universal e-certificate from third parties.
A return-home emergency document may not be accepted for other countries or round trips.
